    \{ \mathsf{labels}~({t_2^\ast}) \} \oplus C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{block}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The notation `\{ \mathsf{labels}~({t^\ast}) \} \oplus C` inserts the new label type at index `0`, shifting all others. The same applies to all other block instructions.

### `\mathsf{loop}~\mathit{blocktype}~\mathit{instr}^\ast`

The instruction `(\mathsf{loop}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast})` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The block type `{\mathit{bt}}` is valid as the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}`.
>
> - Let `{C'}` be the same context as `C`, but with the result type sequence `{t_1^\ast}` prepended to the field `\mathsf{labels}`.
>
> - Under the context `{C'}`, the instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{bt}} : {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    \{ \mathsf{labels}~({t_1^\ast}) \} \oplus C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{loop}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{if}~\mathit{blocktype}~\mathit{instr}_1^\ast~\mathsf{else}~\mathit{instr}_2^\ast`

The instruction `(\mathsf{if}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}~\mathsf{else}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast})` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The block type `{\mathit{bt}}` is valid as the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}`.
>
> - Let `{C'}` be the same context as `C`, but with the result type sequence `{t_2^\ast}` prepended to the field `\mathsf{labels}`.
>
> - Under the context `{C'}`, the instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x_1^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.
>
> - Under the context `{C'}`, the instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x_2^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{bt}} : {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    \{ \mathsf{labels}~({t_2^\ast}) \} \oplus C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x_1^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    \{ \mathsf{labels}~({t_2^\ast}) \} \oplus C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x_2^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{if}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}~\mathsf{else}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast} : {t_1^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{br}~l`

The instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` is of the form `{t^\ast}`.
>
> - The instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l] = {t^\ast}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{br}~l : {t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The label index space in the context `C` contains the most recent label first, so that `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` performs a relative lookup as expected. This applies to other branch instructions as well.

The `\mathsf{br}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

### `\mathsf{br\_if}~l`

The instruction `(\mathsf{br\_if}~l)` is valid with the instruction type `{t^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~{t^\ast}` if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` is of the form `{t^\ast}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l] = {t^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{br\_if}~l : {t^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow {t^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{br\_table}~l^\ast~l_N`

The instruction `(\mathsf{br\_table}~{l^\ast}~{l'})` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - For all `l` in `{l^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>   >
>   > - The result type `{t^\ast}` matches the label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]`.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[{l'}]` exists.
>
> - The result type `{t^\ast}` matches the label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[{l'}]`.
>
> - The instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    (C \vdash {t^\ast} \leq C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l])^\ast
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t^\ast} \leq C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[{l'}]
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{br\_table}~{l^\ast}~{l'} : {t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The `\mathsf{br\_table}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

Furthermore, the result type `{t^\ast}` is also chosen non-deterministically in this rule. Although it may seem necessary to compute `{t^\ast}` as the greatest lower bound of all label types in practice, a simple sequential algorithm does not require this.

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_null}~l`

The instruction `(\mathsf{br\_on\_null}~l)` is valid with the instruction type `{t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}})~\rightarrow~{t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{ht}})` if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` is of the form `{t^\ast}`.
>
> - The heap type `{\mathit{ht}}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l] = {t^\ast}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{ht}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{br\_on\_null}~l : {t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}}) \rightarrow {t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{ht}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_non\_null}~l`

The instruction `(\mathsf{br\_on\_non\_null}~l)` is valid with the instruction type `{t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}})~\rightarrow~{t^\ast}` if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` is of the form `{t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathsf{null}^?}~{\mathit{ht}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l] = {t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathsf{null}^?}~{\mathit{ht}})
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{br\_on\_non\_null}~l : {t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}}) \rightarrow {t^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_cast}~l~\mathit{rt}_1~\mathit{rt}_2`

The instruction `(\mathsf{br\_on\_cast}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2)` is valid with the instruction type `{t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}_1~\rightarrow~{t^\ast}~{\mathit{reftype}}` if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` is of the form `{t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_1` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_2` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_2` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_1`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_2` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{reftype}}` is `{\mathit{rt}}_1 \setminus {\mathit{rt}}_2`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l] = {t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_1 : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_2 : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_2 \leq {\mathit{rt}}_1
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_2 \leq {\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{br\_on\_cast}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2 : {t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}_1 \rightarrow {t^\ast}~({\mathit{rt}}_1 \setminus {\mathit{rt}}_2)
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_cast\_fail}~l~\mathit{rt}_1~\mathit{rt}_2`

The instruction `(\mathsf{br\_on\_cast\_fail}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2)` is valid with the instruction type `{t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}_1~\rightarrow~{t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}_2` if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` is of the form `{t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_1` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_2` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_2` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_1`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_1 \setminus {\mathit{rt}}_2` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l] = {t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_1 : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_2 : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_2 \leq {\mathit{rt}}_1
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_1 \setminus {\mathit{rt}}_2 \leq {\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{br\_on\_cast\_fail}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2 : {t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}_1 \rightarrow {t^\ast}~{\mathit{rt}}_2
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{call}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{call}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The function `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{call}~x : {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{call\_ref}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{call\_ref}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x)~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{call\_ref}~x : {t_1^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x) \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{call\_indirect}~x~y`

The instruction `(\mathsf{call\_indirect}~x~y)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathit{at}}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` matches the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{func})`.
>
> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[y]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[y]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}} \leq (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{func})
    \qquad
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[y] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{call\_indirect}~x~y : {t_1^\ast}~{\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{return}`

The instruction `\mathsf{return}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The result type `C{.}\mathsf{return}` is of the form `{t^\ast}`.
>
> - The instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{return} = ({t^\ast})
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{return} : {t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The `\mathsf{return}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

`C{.}\mathsf{return}` is absent (set to `\epsilon`) when validating an expression that is not a function body. This differs from it being set to the empty result type `{}[\epsilon]`, which is the case for functions not returning anything.

### `\mathsf{return\_call}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{return\_call}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_3^\ast}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_4^\ast}` if:

> - The function `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})`.
>
> - The result type `C{.}\mathsf{return}` is of the form `{{t'}_2^\ast}`.
>
> - The result type `{t_2^\ast}` matches the result type `{{t'}_2^\ast}`.
>
> - The instruction type `{t_3^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_4^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    C{.}\mathsf{return} = ({{t'}_2^\ast})
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_2^\ast} \leq {{t'}_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_3^\ast} \rightarrow {t_4^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{return\_call}~x : {t_3^\ast}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_4^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The `\mathsf{return\_call}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

### `\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_3^\ast}~{t_1^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x)~\rightarrow~{t_4^\ast}` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})`.
>
> - The result type `C{.}\mathsf{return}` is of the form `{{t'}_2^\ast}`.
>
> - The result type `{t_2^\ast}` matches the result type `{{t'}_2^\ast}`.
>
> - The instruction type `{t_3^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_4^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    C{.}\mathsf{return} = ({{t'}_2^\ast})
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_2^\ast} \leq {{t'}_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_3^\ast} \rightarrow {t_4^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~x : {t_3^\ast}~{t_1^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x) \rightarrow {t_4^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The `\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

### `\mathsf{return\_call\_indirect}~x~y`

The instruction `(\mathsf{return\_call\_indirect}~x~y)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_3^\ast}~{t_1^\ast}~{\mathit{at}}~\rightarrow~{t_4^\ast}` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` matches the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{func})`.
>
> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[y]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[y]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})`.
>
> - The result type `C{.}\mathsf{return}` is of the form `{{t'}_2^\ast}`.
>
> - The result type `{t_2^\ast}` matches the result type `{{t'}_2^\ast}`.
>
> - The instruction type `{t_3^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_4^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}} \leq (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{func})
    \\
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[y] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    C{.}\mathsf{return} = ({{t'}_2^\ast})
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_2^\ast} \leq {{t'}_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_3^\ast} \rightarrow {t_4^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    \end{array}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{return\_call\_indirect}~x~y : {t_3^\ast}~{t_1^\ast}~{\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {t_4^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

The `\mathsf{return\_call\_indirect}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

### `\mathsf{throw}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{throw}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The tag `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t^\ast}~\rightarrow)`.
>
> - The instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t^\ast} \rightarrow \epsilon
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{throw}~x : {t_1^\ast}~{t^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The `\mathsf{throw}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

### `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`

The instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{exn})~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{throw\_ref} : {t_1^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{exn}) \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The `\mathsf{throw\_ref}` instruction is stack-polymorphic.

### `\mathsf{try\_table}~\mathit{blocktype}~\mathit{catch}^\ast~\mathit{instr}^\ast`

The instruction `(\mathsf{try\_table}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{catch}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast})` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}` if:

> - The block type `{\mathit{bt}}` is valid as the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast}`.
>
> - Let `{C'}` be the same context as `C`, but with the result type sequence `{t_2^\ast}` prepended to the field `\mathsf{labels}`.
>
> - Under the context `{C'}`, the instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{catch}}` in `{{\mathit{catch}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The catch clause `{\mathit{catch}}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{bt}} : {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    \{ \mathsf{labels}~({t_2^\ast}) \} \oplus C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    (C \vdash {\mathit{catch}} : \mathsf{ok})^\ast
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{try\_table}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{catch}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{catch}~x~l`

The catch clause `(\mathsf{catch}~x~l)` is valid if:

> - The tag `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t^\ast}~\rightarrow)`.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The result type `{t^\ast}` matches the label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t^\ast} \rightarrow \epsilon
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t^\ast} \leq C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{catch}~x~l : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{catch\_ref}~x~l`

The catch clause `(\mathsf{catch\_ref}~x~l)` is valid if:

> - The tag `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t^\ast}~\rightarrow)`.
>
> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The result type `{t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{exn})` matches the label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t^\ast} \rightarrow \epsilon
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{exn}) \leq C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{catch\_ref}~x~l : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{catch\_all}~l`

The catch clause `(\mathsf{catch\_all}~l)` is valid if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The result type `\epsilon` matches the label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash \epsilon \leq C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{catch\_all}~l : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{catch\_all\_ref}~l`

The catch clause `(\mathsf{catch\_all\_ref}~l)` is valid if:

> - The label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]` exists.
>
> - The result type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{exn})` matches the label `C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{exn}) \leq C{.}\mathsf{labels}{}[l]
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{catch\_all\_ref}~l : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Variable Instructions

### `\mathsf{local{.}get}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{local{.}get}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~t` if:

> - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x]` is of the form `(\mathsf{set}~t)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x] = \mathsf{set}~t
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{local{.}get}~x : \epsilon \rightarrow t
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{local{.}set}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{local{.}set}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `t~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{x}\,\epsilon` if:

> - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{init}}~t)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x] = {\mathit{init}}~t
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{local{.}set}~x : t \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{x} \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{local{.}tee}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{local{.}tee}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `t~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{x}\,t` if:

> - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{init}}~t)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x] = {\mathit{init}}~t
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{local{.}tee}~x : t \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{x} t
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{global{.}get}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{global{.}get}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~t` if:

> - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathsf{mut}^?}~t)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x] = {\mathsf{mut}^?}~t
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{global{.}get}~x : \epsilon \rightarrow t
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{global{.}set}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{global{.}set}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `t~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` is of the form `(\mathsf{mut}~t)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x] = \mathsf{mut}~t
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{global{.}set}~x : t \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Table Instructions

### `\mathsf{table{.}get}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}get}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~\rightarrow~{\mathit{rt}}` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table{.}get}~x : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {\mathit{rt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{table{.}set}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}set}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{rt}}~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    }{

    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{table{.}size}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}size}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~{\mathit{at}}` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table{.}size}~x : \epsilon \rightarrow {\mathit{at}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{table{.}grow}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}grow}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{rt}}~{\mathit{at}}~\rightarrow~{\mathit{at}}` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table{.}grow}~x : {\mathit{rt}}~{\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {\mathit{at}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{table{.}fill}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}fill}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{rt}}~{\mathit{at}}~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table{.}fill}~x : {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{rt}}~{\mathit{at}} \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{table{.}copy}~x~y`

The instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}copy}~x_1~x_2)` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}_1~{\mathit{at}}_2~{\mathit{addrtype}}~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x_1]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x_1]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}_1~{\mathit{lim}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_1)`.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x_2]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x_2]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}_2~{\mathit{lim}}_2~{\mathit{rt}}_2)`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_2` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_1`.
>
> - The address type `{\mathit{addrtype}}` is `{\mathrm{min}}({\mathit{at}}_1, {\mathit{at}}_2)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x_1] = {\mathit{at}}_1~{\mathit{lim}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_1
    \qquad
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x_2] = {\mathit{at}}_2~{\mathit{lim}}_2~{\mathit{rt}}_2
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_2 \leq {\mathit{rt}}_1
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table{.}copy}~x_1~x_2 : {\mathit{at}}_1~{\mathit{at}}_2~{\mathrm{min}}({\mathit{at}}_1, {\mathit{at}}_2) \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{table{.}init}~x~y`

The instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}init}~x~y)` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}_1)`.
>
> - The element segment `C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[y]` exists.
>
> - The element segment `C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[y]` is of the form `{\mathit{rt}}_2`.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_2` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}_1`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}_1
    \qquad
    C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[y] = {\mathit{rt}}_2
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}}_2 \leq {\mathit{rt}}_1
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table{.}init}~x~y : {\mathit{at}}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{elem{.}drop}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{elem{.}drop}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The element segment `C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[x]` exists.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[x] = {\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{elem{.}drop}~x : \epsilon \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Memory Instructions

Memory instructions use memory arguments, which are classified by the address type and the and bit width of the access they are suitable for.

### `\mathit{memarg}`

`\{ \mathsf{align}~n,\;\allowbreak \mathsf{offset}~m \}` is valid for `{\mathit{at}}` and `N` if:

> - `{2^{n}}` is less than or equal to `N / 8`.
>
> - `m` is less than `{2^{{|{\mathit{at}}|}}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    {2^{n}} \leq N / 8
    \qquad
    m < {2^{{|{\mathit{at}}|}}}
    }{
    {\vdash}\, \{ \mathsf{align}~n,\;\allowbreak \mathsf{offset}~m \} : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow N
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `t\mathsf{.}\mathsf{load}~x~\mathit{memarg}`

The instruction `({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{load}~x~{\mathit{memarg}})` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~\rightarrow~{\mathit{nt}}` if:

> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page})`.
>
> - `{\mathit{memarg}}` is valid for `{\mathit{at}}` and `{|{\mathit{nt}}|}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page}
    \qquad
    {\vdash}\, {\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {|{\mathit{nt}}|}
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{load}~x~{\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {\mathit{nt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `t\mathsf{.}\mathsf{load}{N}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{sx}~x~\mathit{memarg}`

The instruction `({{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}{.}\mathsf{load}}{{K}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sx}}}}~x~{\mathit{memarg}})` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~\rightarrow~{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}` if:

> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page})`.
>
> - `{\mathit{memarg}}` is valid for `{\mathit{at}}` and `K`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page}
    \qquad
    {\vdash}\, {\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow K
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}{.}\mathsf{load}}{{K}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sx}}}}~x~{\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `t\mathsf{.}\mathsf{store}~x~\mathit{memarg}`

The instruction `({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{store}~x~{\mathit{memarg}})` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{nt}}~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page})`.
>
> - `{\mathit{memarg}}` is valid for `{\mathit{at}}` and `{|{\mathit{nt}}|}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page}
    \qquad
    {\vdash}\, {\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow {|{\mathit{nt}}|}
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{store}~x~{\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{nt}} \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `t\mathsf{.}\mathsf{store}{N}~x~\mathit{memarg}`

The instruction `({{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}{.}\mathsf{store}}{K}~x~{\mathit{memarg}})` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{at}}~{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page})`.
>
> - `{\mathit{memarg}}` is valid for `{\mathit{at}}` and `K`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page}
    \qquad
    {\vdash}\, {\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}} \rightarrow K
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}{.}\mathsf{store}}{K}~x~{\mathit{memarg}} : {\mathit{at}}~{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}} \rightarrow \epsilon
    }

## Reference Instructions

### `\mathsf{ref{.}null}~\mathit{ht}`

The instruction `(\mathsf{ref{.}null}~{\mathit{ht}})` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}})` if:

> - The heap type `{\mathit{ht}}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{ht}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}null}~{\mathit{ht}} : \epsilon \rightarrow (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{ref{.}func}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}})` if:

> - The function `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The function `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` is of the form `{\mathit{dt}}`.
>
> - `x` is contained in `C{.}\mathsf{refs}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x] = {\mathit{dt}}
    \qquad
    x \in C{.}\mathsf{refs}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}func}~x : \epsilon \rightarrow (\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{ref{.}is\_null}`

The instruction `\mathsf{ref{.}is\_null}` is valid with the instruction type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}})~\rightarrow~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` if:

> - The heap type `{\mathit{ht}}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{ht}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}is\_null} : (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}}) \rightarrow \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{ref{.}as\_non\_null}`

The instruction `\mathsf{ref{.}as\_non\_null}` is valid with the instruction type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}})~\rightarrow~(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{ht}})` if:

> - The heap type `{\mathit{ht}}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{ht}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}as\_non\_null} : (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~{\mathit{ht}}) \rightarrow (\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{ht}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{ref{.}eq}`

The instruction `\mathsf{ref{.}eq}` is valid with the instruction type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{eq})~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{eq})~\rightarrow~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}eq} : (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{eq})~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{eq}) \rightarrow \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{ref{.}test}~\mathit{rt}`

The instruction `(\mathsf{ref{.}test}~{\mathit{rt}})` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{rt}'}~\rightarrow~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` if:

> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}'}` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}'}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}'} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}} \leq {\mathit{rt}'}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}test}~{\mathit{rt}} : {\mathit{rt}'} \rightarrow \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The liberty to pick a supertype `{\mathit{rt}'}` allows typing the instruction with the least precise super type of `{\mathit{rt}}` as input, that is, the top type in the corresponding heap subtyping hierarchy.

### `\mathsf{ref{.}cast}~\mathit{rt}`

The instruction `(\mathsf{ref{.}cast}~{\mathit{rt}})` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{rt}'}~\rightarrow~{\mathit{rt}}` if:

> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}'}` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}'}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}'} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}} \leq {\mathit{rt}'}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}cast}~{\mathit{rt}} : {\mathit{rt}'} \rightarrow {\mathit{rt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

The liberty to pick a supertype `{\mathit{rt}'}` allows typing the instruction with the least precise super type of `{\mathit{rt}}` as input, that is, the top type in the corresponding heap subtyping hierarchy.

## Aggregate Reference Instructions

### `\mathsf{struct{.}new}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{struct{.}new}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `{t^\ast}~\rightarrow~(\mathsf{ref}~x)` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{struct}~{({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})^\ast})`.
>
> - The value type sequence `{t^\ast}` is `{{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})^\ast}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{struct}~{({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{struct{.}new}~x : {{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})^\ast} \rightarrow (\mathsf{ref}~x)
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{struct{.}new\_default}~x`

The instruction `(\mathsf{struct{.}new\_default}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~(\mathsf{ref}~x)` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{struct}~{({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})^\ast})`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{zt}}` in `{{\mathit{zt}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - A default value for `{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})` is defined.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{struct}~{({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})^\ast}
    \qquad
    ({{\mathrm{default}}}_{{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})} \neq \epsilon)^\ast
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{struct{.}new\_default}~x : \epsilon \rightarrow (\mathsf{ref}~x)
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{struct{.}get}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{sx}^?~x~y`

The instruction `({\mathsf{struct{.}get}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{{\mathit{sx}}^?}}~x~i)` is valid with the instruction type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x)~\rightarrow~t` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{struct}~{{\mathit{ft}}^\ast})`.
>
> - The length of `{{\mathit{ft}}^\ast}` is greater than `i`.
>
> - The field type `{{\mathit{ft}}^\ast}{}[i]` is of the form `({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})`.
>
> - The signedness `{{\mathit{sx}}^?}` is present if and only if `{\mathit{zt}}` is a packed type.
>
> - The value type `t` is `{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{struct}~{{\mathit{ft}}^\ast}
    \qquad
    {{\mathit{ft}}^\ast}{}[i] = {\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}}
    \qquad
    {{\mathit{sx}}^?} \neq \epsilon \Leftrightarrow {\mathit{zt}} \neq {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathsf{struct{.}get}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{{\mathit{sx}}^?}}~x~i : (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x) \rightarrow {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{struct{.}set}~x~y`

The instruction `(\mathsf{struct{.}set}~x~i)` is valid with the instruction type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x)~t~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

>
> - The field type `{{\mathit{ft}}^\ast}{}[i]` is of the form `(\mathsf{mut}~{\mathit{zt}})`.
>
> - The value type `t` is `{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})`.

    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{struct}~{{\mathit{ft}}^\ast}
    \qquad
    {{\mathit{ft}}^\ast}{}[i] = \mathsf{mut}~{\mathit{zt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{struct{.}set}~x~i : (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x)~{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}}) \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{rt}}))`.
>
> - The element segment `C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[y]` exists.
>
> - The element segment `C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[y]` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{rt}})
    \qquad
    C \vdash C{.}\mathsf{elems}{}[y] \leq {\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{array{.}new\_elem}~x~y : \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow (\mathsf{ref}~x)
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{array{.}new\_data}~x~y`

The instruction `(\mathsf{array{.}new\_data}~x~y)` is valid with the instruction type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~(\mathsf{ref}~x)` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}}))`.
>
> - The value type `{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})` is of the form `{\mathit{numtype}}` or `{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})` is of the form `{\mathit{vectype}}`.
>
> - The data segment `C{.}\mathsf{datas}{}[y]` exists.
>
> - The data segment `C{.}\mathsf{datas}{}[y]` is of the form `\mathsf{ok}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})
    \qquad
    {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}}) = {\mathit{numtype}} \lor {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}}) = {\mathit{vectype}}
    \qquad
    C{.}\mathsf{datas}{}[y] = \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{array{.}new\_data}~x~y : \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow (\mathsf{ref}~x)
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{array{.}get}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{sx}^?~x`

The instruction `({\mathsf{array{.}get}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{{\mathit{sx}}^?}}~x)` is valid with the instruction type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x)~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~t` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}}))`.
>
> - The signedness `{{\mathit{sx}}^?}` is present if and only if `{\mathit{zt}}` is a packed type.
>
> - The value type `t` is `{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})
    \qquad
    {{\mathit{sx}}^?} \neq \epsilon \Leftrightarrow {\mathit{zt}} \neq {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathsf{array{.}get}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{{\mathit{sx}}^?}}~x : (\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x)~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

The instruction `(\mathsf{array{.}copy}~x_1~x_2)` is valid with the instruction type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x_1)~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~x_2)~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\rightarrow~\epsilon` if:

    C \vdash {\mathit{zt}}_2 \leq {\mathit{zt}}_1

## Vector Instructions

Vector instructions can have a prefix to describe the shape of the operand. Packed numeric types, `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle8}` and `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle16}`, are not value types. An auxiliary function maps such packed type shapes to value types:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{unpack}}({{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}) & = & {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathit{ishape}_1\mathsf{.}\mathit{vextbinop}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{ishape}_2`

The instruction `({\mathit{sh}}_1 {.} {{\mathit{vextbinop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2})` is valid with the instruction type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\rightarrow~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{sh}}_1 {.} {{\mathit{vextbinop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2} : \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128} \rightarrow \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathit{ishape}_1\mathsf{.}\mathit{vextternop}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{ishape}_2`

The instruction `({\mathit{sh}}_1 {.} {{\mathit{vextternop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2})` is valid with the instruction type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\rightarrow~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{sh}}_1 {.} {{\mathit{vextternop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2} : \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128} \rightarrow \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathit{ishape}_1\mathsf{.}\mathsf{narrow}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{ishape}_2\mathsf{\_}\mathit{sx}`

The instruction `({{\mathit{sh}}_1{.}\mathsf{narrow}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sx}}})` is valid with the instruction type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\rightarrow~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{sh}}_1{.}\mathsf{narrow}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sx}}} : \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128} \rightarrow \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathit{shape}\mathsf{.}\mathit{vcvtop}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{half}^?\mathsf{\_}\mathit{shape}\mathsf{\_}\mathit{sx}^?\mathsf{\_zero}^?`

The instruction `({\mathit{sh}}_1 {.} {{\mathit{vcvtop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2})` is valid with the instruction type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}~\rightarrow~\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{sh}}_1 {.} {{\mathit{vcvtop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_2} : \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128} \rightarrow \mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Instruction Sequences

Typing of instruction sequences is defined recursively.

The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{it}}` if:

> - Either:
>
>   > - The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is empty.
>   >
>   > - The instruction type `{\mathit{it}}` is of the form `\epsilon~\rightarrow~\epsilon`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathit{instr}'}`.
>   >
>   > - The instruction type `{\mathit{it}}` is of the form `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}'}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is of the form `{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The instruction type `{\mathit{it}}` is of the form `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x_1^\ast}~{x_2^\ast}}\,{t_3^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x_1^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - For all `x_1` in `{x_1^\ast}`:
>   >
>   >   > - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x_1]` exists.
>   >   >
>   >   > - The local `C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x_1]` is of the form `({\mathit{init}}~t)`.
>   >
>   > - Under the context `C` with the local types of `{x_1^\ast}` updated to `{(\mathsf{set}~t)^\ast}`, the instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_2^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x_2^\ast}}\,{t_3^\ast}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{\mathit{it}''}`.
>   >
>   > - The instruction type `{\mathit{it}''}` matches the instruction type `{\mathit{it}}`.
>   >
>   > - The instruction type `{\mathit{it}}` is valid.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction type `{\mathit{it}}` is of the form `{t^\ast}~{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x^\ast}}\,{t^\ast}~{t_2^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `{t_1^\ast}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{x^\ast}}\,{t_2^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The result type `{t^\ast}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash \epsilon : \epsilon \rightarrow \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{instr}} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{instr}} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x_1^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    (C{.}\mathsf{locals}{}[x_1] = {\mathit{init}}~t)^\ast
    \qquad
    C{}[{.}\mathsf{local}{}[{x_1^\ast}] = {(\mathsf{set}~t)^\ast}] \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast} : {t_2^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x_2^\ast}} {t_3^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x_1^\ast}~{x_2^\ast}} {t_3^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {\mathit{it}}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{it}} \leq {\mathit{it}'}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{it}'} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {\mathit{it}'}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

This *subsumption rule* allows to weaken the type of an instruction sequence to a supertype, which includes the ability to drop init variables `{x^\ast}` from the instruction type in a context where they are not needed, for example, at the end of the body of a block.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t_1^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x^\ast}} {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {t^\ast} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : ({t^\ast}~{t_1^\ast}) \mathrel{\rightarrow}_{{x^\ast}} ({t^\ast}~{t_2^\ast})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

In combination with the previous two rules, this *frame rule* allows to compose instructions whose types would not directly fit otherwise. For example, consider the instruction sequence

    (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~1)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~2)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} {.} \mathsf{add})

To type this sequence, its subsequence `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~2)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} {.} \mathsf{add})` needs to be valid with an intermediate type. But the direct type of `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~2)` is `\epsilon \rightarrow \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}`, not matching the two inputs expected by `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} {.} \mathsf{add}`. The rule allows to weaken the type of `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~2)` to the supertype `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}`, such that it can be composed with `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} {.} \mathsf{add}` and yields the intermediate type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \rightarrow \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` for the subsequence. That can in turn be composed with the first constant.

## Expressions

Expressions `{\mathit{expr}}` are classified by result types `{t^\ast}`.

The expression `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is valid with the result type `{t^\ast}` if:

> - The instruction sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is valid with the instruction type `\epsilon~\rightarrow~{t^\ast}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : \epsilon \rightarrow {t^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} : {t^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Constant Expressions

In a *constant* expression, all instructions must be constant.

`{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` is constant if:

> - For all `{\mathit{instr}}` in `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - `{\mathit{instr}}` is constant.

`{\mathit{instr}}` is constant if:

> - Either:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_{\mathit{nt}})`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `({\mathit{vt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_{\mathit{vt}})`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{ref{.}null}~{\mathit{ht}})`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `\mathsf{ref{.}i\scriptstyle31}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~x)`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{struct{.}new}~x)`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{struct{.}new\_default}~x)`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{array{.}new}~x)`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{array{.}new\_default}~x)`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{array{.}new\_fixed}~x~n)`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `\mathsf{any{.}convert\_extern}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `\mathsf{extern{.}convert\_any}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{global{.}get}~x)`.
>   >
>   > - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` exists.
>   >
>   > - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` is of the form `(\epsilon~t)`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The instruction `{\mathit{instr}}` is of the form `({\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}} {.} {\mathit{binop}})`.
>   >
>   > - `{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}` is contained in \[`\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}`; `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle64}`\].
>   >
>   > - `{\mathit{binop}}` is contained in \[`\mathsf{add}`; `\mathsf{sub}`; `\mathsf{mul}`\].

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    (C \vdash {\mathit{instr}}~\mathsf{const})^\ast
    }{
    C \vdash {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_{\mathit{nt}})~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash ({\mathit{vt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_{\mathit{vt}})~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    {\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}} \in \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle64}
    \qquad
    {\mathit{binop}} \in \mathsf{add}~\mathsf{sub}~\mathsf{mul}
    }{
    C \vdash ({\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}} {.} {\mathit{binop}})~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \\[3ex]\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{ref{.}null}~{\mathit{ht}})~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{ref{.}i\scriptstyle31})~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{ref{.}func}~x)~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \\[3ex]\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{struct{.}new}~x)~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{struct{.}new\_default}~x)~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \\[3ex]\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{array{.}new}~x)~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{array{.}new\_default}~x)~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{array{.}new\_fixed}~x~n)~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \\[3ex]\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{any{.}convert\_extern})~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{extern{.}convert\_any})~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \\[3ex]\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x] = t
    }{
    C \vdash (\mathsf{global{.}get}~x)~\mathsf{const}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Currently, constant expressions occurring in globals are further constrained in that contained `\mathsf{global{.}get}` instructions are only allowed to refer to *imported* or *previously defined* globals. Constant expressions occurring in tables may only have `\mathsf{global{.}get}` instructions that refer to *imported* globals. This is enforced in the validation rule for modules by constraining the context `C` accordingly.

The definition of constant expression may be extended in future versions of WebAssembly.

# Modules

Modules are valid when all the components they contain are valid. To verify this, most definitions are themselves classified with a suitable type.

## Types

The sequence of types defined in a module is validated incrementally, yielding a sequence of defined types representing them individually.

The type definition `(\mathsf{type}~{\mathit{rectype}})` is valid with the defined type sequence `{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}` if:

> - The length of `C{.}\mathsf{types}` is equal to `x`.
>
> - The defined type sequence `{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}` is of the form `{{{{\mathrm{roll}}}_{x}^\ast}}{({\mathit{rectype}})}`.
>
> - Let `{C'}` be the same context as `C`, but with the defined type sequence `{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}` appended to the field `\mathsf{types}`.
>
> - Under the context `{C'}`, the recursive type `{\mathit{rectype}}` is valid for the type index `x`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    x = {|C{.}\mathsf{types}|}
    \qquad
    {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} = {{{{\mathrm{roll}}}_{x}^\ast}}{({\mathit{rectype}})}
    \qquad
    C \oplus \{ \mathsf{types}~{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} \} \vdash {\mathit{rectype}} : {\mathsf{ok}}{(x)}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{rectype}} : {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

The type definition sequence `{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}` is valid with the defined type sequence `{{\mathit{deftype}}^\ast}` if:

> - Either:
>
>   > - The type definition sequence `{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}` is empty.
>   >
>   > - The defined type sequence `{{\mathit{deftype}}^\ast}` is empty.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The type definition sequence `{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathit{type}}_1~{{\mathit{type}'}^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The defined type sequence `{{\mathit{deftype}}^\ast}` is of the form `{{\mathit{dt}}_1^\ast}~{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The type definition `{\mathit{type}}_1` is valid with the defined type sequence `{{\mathit{dt}}_1^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - Let `{C'}` be the same context as `C`, but with the defined type sequence `{{\mathit{dt}}_1^\ast}` appended to the field `\mathsf{types}`.
>   >
>   > - Under the context `{C'}`, the type definition sequence `{{\mathit{type}'}^\ast}` is valid with the defined type sequence `{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash \epsilon : \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{type}}_1 : {{\mathit{dt}}_1^\ast}
    \qquad
    C \oplus \{ \mathsf{types}~{{\mathit{dt}}_1^\ast} \} \vdash {{\mathit{type}}^\ast} : {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{type}}_1~{{\mathit{type}}^\ast} : {{\mathit{dt}}_1^\ast}~{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Tags

Tags `\mathit{tag}` are classified by their tag types, which are defined types expanding to function types.

The tag `(\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{tagtype}})` is valid with the tag type `{\mathit{tagtype}'}` if:

> - The tag type `{\mathit{tagtype}}` is valid.
>
> - The tag type `{\mathit{tagtype}'}` is `{{\mathsf{clos}}}_{C}({\mathit{tagtype}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{tagtype}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{tagtype}} : {{\mathsf{clos}}}_{C}({\mathit{tagtype}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Globals

Globals `{\mathit{global}}` are classified by global types.

The global `(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globaltype}}~{\mathit{expr}})` is valid with the global type `{\mathit{globaltype}}` if:

> - The global type `{\mathit{globaltype}}` is valid.
>
> - The global type `{\mathit{globaltype}}` is of the form `({\mathsf{mut}^?}~t)`.
>
> - The expression `{\mathit{expr}}` is valid with the value type `t`.
>
> - `{\mathit{expr}}` is constant.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{globaltype}} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    {\mathit{globaltype}} = {\mathsf{mut}^?}~t
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{expr}} : t~\mathsf{const}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globaltype}}~{\mathit{expr}} : {\mathit{globaltype}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Sequences of globals are handled incrementally, such that each definition has access to previous definitions.

The global sequence `{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}` is valid with the global type sequence `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}` if:

> - Either:
>
>   > - The global sequence `{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}` is empty.
>   >
>   > - The global type sequence `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}` is empty.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The global sequence `{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathit{global}}_1~{{\mathit{global}'}^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The global type sequence `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathit{gt}}_1~{{\mathit{gt}}^\ast}`.
>   >
>   > - The global `{\mathit{global}}_1` is valid with the global type `{\mathit{gt}}_1`.
>   >
>   > - Let `{C'}` be the same context as `C`, but with the global type sequence `{\mathit{gt}}_1` appended to the field `\mathsf{globals}`.
>   >
>   > - Under the context `{C'}`, the global sequence `{{\mathit{global}'}^\ast}` is valid with the global type sequence `{{\mathit{gt}}^\ast}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash \epsilon : \epsilon
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{global}}_1 : {\mathit{gt}}_1
    \qquad
    C \oplus \{ \mathsf{globals}~{\mathit{gt}}_1 \} \vdash {{\mathit{global}}^\ast} : {{\mathit{gt}}^\ast}
    }{
    C \vdash {\mathit{global}}_1~{{\mathit{global}}^\ast} : {\mathit{gt}}_1~{{\mathit{gt}}^\ast}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Memories

Memories `{\mathit{mem}}` are classified by memory types.

The memory `(\mathsf{memory}~{\mathit{memtype}})` is valid with the memory type `{\mathit{memtype}}` if:

> - The memory type `{\mathit{memtype}}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{memtype}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{memory}~{\mathit{memtype}} : {\mathit{memtype}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Tables

Tables `{\mathit{table}}` are classified by table types.

The table `(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tabletype}}~{\mathit{expr}})` is valid with the table type `{\mathit{tabletype}}` if:

> - The table type `{\mathit{tabletype}}` is valid.
>
> - The table type `{\mathit{tabletype}}` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}})`.
>
> - The expression `{\mathit{expr}}` is valid with the value type `{\mathit{rt}}`.
>
> - `{\mathit{expr}}` is constant.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{tabletype}} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    {\mathit{tabletype}} = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{expr}} : {\mathit{rt}}~\mathsf{const}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tabletype}}~{\mathit{expr}} : {\mathit{tabletype}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Functions

Functions `{\mathit{func}}` are classified by defined types that expand to function types of the form `\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}`.

The function `(\mathsf{func}~x~{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}~{\mathit{expr}})` is valid with the type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` if:

> - The type `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{local}}` in `{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The local `{\mathit{local}}` is valid with the local type `{{\mathit{lt}}}`.
>
> - `{{{\mathit{lt}}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{{\mathit{lt}}}`.
>
> - Under the context `C` with the field `\mathsf{locals}` appended by `{(\mathsf{set}~t_1)^\ast}~{{{\mathit{lt}}}^\ast}` and the field `\mathsf{labels}` appended by `{t_2^\ast}` and the field `\mathsf{return}` appended by `{t_2^\ast}`, the expression `{\mathit{expr}}` is valid with the result type `{t_2^\ast}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}
    C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast}
    \qquad
    (C \vdash {\mathit{local}} : {{\mathit{lt}}})^\ast
    \\
    C \oplus \{ \mathsf{locals}~{(\mathsf{set}~t_1)^\ast}~{{{\mathit{lt}}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{labels}~({t_2^\ast}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{return}~({t_2^\ast}) \} \vdash {\mathit{expr}} : {t_2^\ast}
    \end{array}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{func}~x~{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}~{\mathit{expr}} : C{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}\end{split}

## Locals

Locals `{\mathit{local}}` are classified with local types.

The local `(\mathsf{local}~t)` is valid with the local type `({\mathit{init}}~t)` if:

> - The value type `t` is valid.
>
> - Either:
>
>   > - The initialization status `{\mathit{init}}` is of the form `\mathsf{set}`.
>   >
>   > - A default value for `t` is defined.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The initialization status `{\mathit{init}}` is of the form `\mathsf{unset}`.
>   >
>   > - A default value for `t` is not defined.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash t : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    {{\mathrm{default}}}_{t} \neq \epsilon
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{local}~t : \mathsf{set}~t
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    C \vdash t : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    {{\mathrm{default}}}_{t} = \epsilon
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{local}~t : \mathsf{unset}~t
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

For cases where both rules are applicable, the former yields the more permissable type.

## Data Segments

Data segments `{\mathit{data}}` are classified by the singleton data type, which merely expresses well-formedness.

The memory segment `(\mathsf{data}~{b^\ast}~{\mathit{datamode}})` is valid if:

> - The data mode `{\mathit{datamode}}` is valid.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{datamode}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{data}~{b^\ast}~{\mathit{datamode}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

The data mode `{\mathit{datamode}}` is valid if:

> - Either:
>
>   > - The data mode `{\mathit{datamode}}` is of the form `\mathsf{passive}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The data mode `{\mathit{datamode}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{active}~x~{\mathit{expr}})`.
>   >
>   > - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` exists.
>   >
>   > - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page})`.
>   >
>   > - The expression `{\mathit{expr}}` is valid with the value type `{\mathit{at}}`.
>   >
>   > - `{\mathit{expr}}` is constant.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{passive} : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~\mathsf{page}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{expr}} : {\mathit{at}}~\mathsf{const}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{active}~x~{\mathit{expr}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Element Segments

Element segments `{\mathit{elem}}` are classified by their element type.

The table segment `(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{elemtype}}~{{\mathit{expr}}^\ast}~{\mathit{elemmode}})` is valid with the element type `{\mathit{elemtype}}` if:

> - The reference type `{\mathit{elemtype}}` is valid.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{expr}}` in `{{\mathit{expr}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The expression `{\mathit{expr}}` is valid with the value type `{\mathit{elemtype}}`.
>   >
>   > - `{\mathit{expr}}` is constant.
>
> - The element mode `{\mathit{elemmode}}` is valid with the element type `{\mathit{elemtype}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{elemtype}} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    (C \vdash {\mathit{expr}} : {\mathit{elemtype}}~\mathsf{const})^\ast
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{elemmode}} : {\mathit{elemtype}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{elemtype}}~{{\mathit{expr}}^\ast}~{\mathit{elemmode}} : {\mathit{elemtype}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

The element mode `{\mathit{elemmode}}` is valid with the element type `{\mathit{rt}}` if:

> - Either:
>
>   > - The element mode `{\mathit{elemmode}}` is of the form `\mathsf{passive}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The element mode `{\mathit{elemmode}}` is of the form `\mathsf{declare}`.
>
> - Or:
>
>   > - The element mode `{\mathit{elemmode}}` is of the form `(\mathsf{active}~x~{\mathit{expr}})`.
>   >
>   > - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>   >
>   > - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `({\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}'})`.
>   >
>   > - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}'}`.
>   >
>   > - The expression `{\mathit{expr}}` is valid with the value type `{\mathit{at}}`.
>   >
>   > - `{\mathit{expr}}` is constant.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{passive} : {\mathit{rt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \frac{
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{declare} : {\mathit{rt}}
    }
    \\[3ex]\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{at}}~{\mathit{lim}}~{\mathit{rt}'}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{rt}} \leq {\mathit{rt}'}
    \qquad
    C \vdash {\mathit{expr}} : {\mathit{at}}~\mathsf{const}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{active}~x~{\mathit{expr}} : {\mathit{rt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}\end{split}

## Start Function

The start function `(\mathsf{start}~x)` is valid if:

> - The function `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The expansion of `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` is `(\mathsf{func}~\rightarrow)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~\epsilon \rightarrow \epsilon
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{start}~x : \mathsf{ok}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Imports

Imports `{\mathit{import}}` are classified by external types.

The import `(\mathsf{import}~{\mathit{name}}_1~{\mathit{name}}_2~{\mathit{xt}})` is valid with the external type `{\mathit{externtype}}` if:

> - The external type `{\mathit{xt}}` is valid.
>
> - The external type `{\mathit{externtype}}` is `{{\mathsf{clos}}}_{C}({\mathit{xt}})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{xt}} : \mathsf{ok}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{import}~{\mathit{name}}_1~{\mathit{name}}_2~{\mathit{xt}} : {{\mathsf{clos}}}_{C}({\mathit{xt}})
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Exports

Exports `{\mathit{export}}` are classified by their external type.

The export `(\mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~{\mathit{externidx}})` is valid with the name `{\mathit{name}}` and the external type `{\mathit{xt}}` if:

> - The external index `{\mathit{externidx}}` is valid with the external type `{\mathit{xt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C \vdash {\mathit{externidx}} : {\mathit{xt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~{\mathit{externidx}} : {\mathit{name}}~{\mathit{xt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{tag}~x`

The external index `(\mathsf{tag}~x)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{jt}})` if:

> - The tag `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The tag `C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]` is of the form `{\mathit{jt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x] = {\mathit{jt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{tag}~x : \mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{jt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{global}~x`

The external index `(\mathsf{global}~x)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{gt}})` if:

> - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The global `C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]` is of the form `{\mathit{gt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x] = {\mathit{gt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{global}~x : \mathsf{global}~{\mathit{gt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{memory}~x`

The external index `(\mathsf{memory}~x)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{mem}~{\mathit{mt}})` if:

> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The memory `C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]` is of the form `{\mathit{mt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x] = {\mathit{mt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{memory}~x : \mathsf{mem}~{\mathit{mt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{table}~x`

The external index `(\mathsf{table}~x)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tt}})` if:

> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The table `C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]` is of the form `{\mathit{tt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x] = {\mathit{tt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{table}~x : \mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### `\mathsf{func}~x`

The external index `(\mathsf{func}~x)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{dt}})` if:

> - The function `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` exists.
>
> - The function `C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]` is of the form `{\mathit{dt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    C{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x] = {\mathit{dt}}
    }{
    C \vdash \mathsf{func}~x : \mathsf{func}~{\mathit{dt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## Modules

Modules are classified by their mapping from the external types of their imports to those of their exports.

A module is entirely *closed*, that is, its components can only refer to definitions that appear in the module itself. Consequently, no initial context is required. Instead, the context `C` for validation of the module’s content is constructed from the definitions in the module.

The module `(\mathsf{module}~{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{import}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{tag}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{start}}^?}~{{\mathit{export}}^\ast})` is valid with the module type `{\mathit{moduletype}}` if:

> - Under the context `\{ \mathsf{return}~\epsilon \}`, the type definition sequence `{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}` is valid with the defined type sequence `{{\mathit{dt}'}^\ast}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{import}}` in `{{\mathit{import}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - Under the context `\{ \mathsf{types}~{{\mathit{dt}'}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{return}~\epsilon \}`, the import `{\mathit{import}}` is valid with the external type `{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{tag}}` in `{{\mathit{tag}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - Under the context `{C'}`, the tag `{\mathit{tag}}` is valid with the tag type `{\mathit{jt}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{jt}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{jt}}`.
>
> - Under the context `{C'}`, the global sequence `{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}` is valid with the global type sequence `{{\mathit{gt}}^\ast}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{mem}}` in `{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - Under the context `{C'}`, the memory `{\mathit{mem}}` is valid with the memory type `{\mathit{mt}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{mt}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{mt}}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{table}}` in `{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - Under the context `{C'}`, the table `{\mathit{table}}` is valid with the table type `{\mathit{tt}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{tt}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{tt}}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{func}}` in `{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The function `{\mathit{func}}` is valid with the defined type `{\mathit{dt}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{dt}}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{data}}` in `{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The memory segment `{\mathit{data}}` is valid.
>
> - `{{\mathit{ok}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{ok}}`.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{elem}}` in `{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The table segment `{\mathit{elem}}` is valid with the element type `{\mathit{rt}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{rt}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{rt}}`.
>
> - If `{\mathit{start}}` is defined, then:
>
>   > - The start function `{\mathit{start}}` is valid.
>
> - For all `{\mathit{export}}` in `{{\mathit{export}}^\ast}`:
>
>   > - The export `{\mathit{export}}` is valid with the name `{\mathit{nm}}` and the external type `{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{e}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{nm}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{nm}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}` is the concatenation of all such `{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{e}}`.
>
> - `{{\mathit{nm}}^\ast}~{\mathrm{disjoint}}` is true.
>
> - The context `C` is of the form `{C'}` with the field `\mathsf{tags}` appended by `{{\mathit{jt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{jt}}^\ast}` and the field `\mathsf{globals}` appended by `{{\mathit{gt}}^\ast}` and the field `\mathsf{mems}` appended by `{{\mathit{mt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{mt}}^\ast}` and the field `\mathsf{tables}` appended by `{{\mathit{tt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{tt}}^\ast}` and the field `\mathsf{datas}` appended by `{{\mathit{ok}}^\ast}` and the field `\mathsf{elems}` appended by `{{\mathit{rt}}^\ast}`.
>
> - The context `{C'}` is of the form `\{ \mathsf{types}~{{\mathit{dt}'}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{globals}~{{\mathit{gt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{funcs}~{{\mathit{dt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{return}~\epsilon,\;\allowbreak \mathsf{refs}~{x^\ast} \}`.
>
> - The function index sequence `{x^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathrm{funcidx}}({{\mathit{global}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{export}}^\ast})`.
>
> - The tag type sequence `{{\mathit{jt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathrm{tags}}({{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast})`.
>
> - The global type sequence `{{\mathit{gt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathrm{globals}}({{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast})`.
>
> - The memory type sequence `{{\mathit{mt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathrm{mems}}({{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast})`.
>
> - The table type sequence `{{\mathit{tt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` is of the form `{\mathrm{tables}}({{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast})`.
>
