    \mathrm{fmax}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2\} \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_1\} \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(+ \infty, z_2) &=& + \infty \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(- \infty, z_2) &=& z_2 \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, + \infty) &=& + \infty \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, - \infty) &=& z_1 \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& +0 \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& z_1 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} z_1 \geq z_2) \\
    \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& z_2 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} z_2 \geq z_1) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fcopysign}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If `z_1` and `z_2` have the same sign, then return `z_1`.

- Else return `z_1` with negated sign.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fcopysign}_N(\pm p_1, \pm p_2) &=& \pm p_1 \\
    \mathrm{fcopysign}_N(\pm p_1, \mp p_2) &=& \mp p_1 \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fabs}_N(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return `z` with positive sign.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then return positive infinity.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return positive zero.

- Else if `z` is a positive value, then `z`.

- Else return `z` negated.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fabs}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& +\mathsf{nan}(n) \\
    \mathrm{fabs}_N(\pm \infty) &=& +\infty \\
    \mathrm{fabs}_N(\pm 0) &=& +0 \\
    \mathrm{fabs}_N(\pm q) &=& +q \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fneg}_N(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return `z` with negated sign.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then return that infinity negated.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return that zero negated.

- Else return `z` negated.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fneg}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mp \mathsf{nan}(n) \\
    \mathrm{fneg}_N(\pm \infty) &=& \mp \infty \\
    \mathrm{fneg}_N(\pm 0) &=& \mp 0 \\
    \mathrm{fneg}_N(\pm q) &=& \mp q \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fsqrt}_N(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{z\}`.

- Else if `z` is negative infinity, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{\}`.

- Else if `z` is positive infinity, then return positive infinity.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return that zero.

- Else if `z` has a negative sign, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{\}`.

- Else return the square root of `z`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fsqrt}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)\} \\
    \mathrm{fsqrt}_N(- \infty) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\} \\
    \mathrm{fsqrt}_N(+ \infty) &=& + \infty \\
    \mathrm{fsqrt}_N(\pm 0) &=& \pm 0 \\
    \mathrm{fsqrt}_N(- q) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\} \\
    \mathrm{fsqrt}_N(+ q) &=& \mathrm{float}_N\left(\sqrt{q}\right) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fceil}_N(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{z\}`.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is smaller than `0` but greater than `-1`, then return negative zero.

- Else return the smallest integral value that is not smaller than `z`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fceil}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)\} \\
    \mathrm{fceil}_N(\pm \infty) &=& \pm \infty \\
    \mathrm{fceil}_N(\pm 0) &=& \pm 0 \\
    \mathrm{fceil}_N(- q) &=& -0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} -1 < -q < 0) \\
    \mathrm{fceil}_N(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(i) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} \pm q \leq i < \pm q + 1) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{ffloor}_N(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{z\}`.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is greater than `0` but smaller than `1`, then return positive zero.

- Else return the largest integral value that is not larger than `z`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ffloor}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)\} \\
    \mathrm{ffloor}_N(\pm \infty) &=& \pm \infty \\
    \mathrm{ffloor}_N(\pm 0) &=& \pm 0 \\
    \mathrm{ffloor}_N(+ q) &=& +0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} 0 < +q < 1) \\
    \mathrm{ffloor}_N(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(i) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} \pm q - 1 < i \leq \pm q) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{ftrunc}_N(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{z\}`.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is greater than `0` but smaller than `1`, then return positive zero.

- Else if `z` is smaller than `0` but greater than `-1`, then return negative zero.

- Else return the integral value with the same sign as `z` and the largest magnitude that is not larger than the magnitude of `z`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ftrunc}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)\} \\
    \mathrm{ftrunc}_N(\pm \infty) &=& \pm \infty \\
    \mathrm{ftrunc}_N(\pm 0) &=& \pm 0 \\
    \mathrm{ftrunc}_N(+ q) &=& +0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} 0 < +q < 1) \\
    \mathrm{ftrunc}_N(- q) &=& -0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} -1 < -q < 0) \\
    \mathrm{ftrunc}_N(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(\pm i) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} +q - 1 < i \leq +q) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fnearest}_N(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{z\}`.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return `z`.

- Else if `z` is greater than `0` but smaller than or equal to `0.5`, then return positive zero.

- Else if `z` is smaller than `0` but greater than or equal to `-0.5`, then return negative zero.

- Else return the integral value that is nearest to `z`; if two values are equally near, return the even one.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fnearest}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)\} \\
    \mathrm{fnearest}_N(\pm \infty) &=& \pm \infty \\
    \mathrm{fnearest}_N(\pm 0) &=& \pm 0 \\
    \mathrm{fnearest}_N(+ q) &=& +0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} 0 < +q \leq 0.5) \\
    \mathrm{fnearest}_N(- q) &=& -0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} -0.5 \leq -q < 0) \\
    \mathrm{fnearest}_N(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(\pm i) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} |i - q| < 0.5) \\
    \mathrm{fnearest}_N(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(\pm i) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} |i - q| = 0.5 \wedge i~\mbox{even}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{feq}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If either `z_1` or `z_2` is a NaN, then return `0`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes, then return `1`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are the same value, then return `1`.

- Else return `0`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{feq}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{feq}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{feq}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{feq}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{bool}(z_1 = z_2) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fne}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If either `z_1` or `z_2` is a NaN, then return `1`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes, then return `0`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are the same value, then return `0`.

- Else return `1`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fne}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fne}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fne}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fne}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{bool}(z_1 \neq z_2) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{flt}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If either `z_1` or `z_2` is a NaN, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` and `z_2` are the same value, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` is positive infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` is negative infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_2` is positive infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_2` is negative infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` is smaller than `z_2`, then return `1`.

- Else return `0`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{flt}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(z, z) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(+ \infty, z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(- \infty, z_2) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(z_1, + \infty) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(z_1, - \infty) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{flt}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{bool}(z_1 < z_2) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fgt}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If either `z_1` or `z_2` is a NaN, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` and `z_2` are the same value, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` is positive infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_1` is negative infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_2` is positive infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_2` is negative infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` is larger than `z_2`, then return `1`.

- Else return `0`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(z, z) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(+ \infty, z_2) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(- \infty, z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(z_1, + \infty) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(z_1, - \infty) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fgt}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{bool}(z_1 > z_2) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fle}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If either `z_1` or `z_2` is a NaN, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` and `z_2` are the same value, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_1` is positive infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` is negative infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_2` is positive infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_2` is negative infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_1` is smaller than or equal to `z_2`, then return `1`.

- Else return `0`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fle}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(z, z) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(+ \infty, z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(- \infty, z_2) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(z_1, + \infty) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(z_1, - \infty) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fle}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{bool}(z_1 \leq z_2) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fge}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If either `z_1` or `z_2` is a NaN, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_1` and `z_2` are the same value, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_1` is positive infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_1` is negative infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_2` is positive infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if `z_2` is negative infinity, then return `1`.

- Else if both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes, then return `1`.

- Else if `z_1` is larger than or equal to `z_2`, then return `1`.

- Else return `0`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fge}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(z, z) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(+ \infty, z_2) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(- \infty, z_2) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(z_1, + \infty) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(z_1, - \infty) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& 1 \\
    \mathrm{fge}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{bool}(z_1 \geq z_2) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fpmin}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If `z_2` is less than `z_1` then return `z_2`.

- Else return `z_1`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fpmin}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& z_2 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} \mathrm{flt}_N(z_2, z_1) = 1) \\
    \mathrm{fpmin}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& z_1 & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}})
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{fpmax}_N(z_1, z_2)`

- If `z_1` is less than `z_2` then return `z_2`.

- Else return `z_1`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{fpmax}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& z_2 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} \mathrm{flt}_N(z_1, z_2) = 1) \\
    \mathrm{fpmax}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& z_1 & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}})
    \end{array}\end{split}

## Conversions

### `\mathrm{extend}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(i)`

- Return `i`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{extend}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(i) &=& i \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

In the abstract syntax, unsigned extension just reinterprets the same value.

### `\mathrm{extend}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(i)`

- Let `j` be the signed interpretation of `i` of size `M`.

- Return the two’s complement of `j` relative to size `N`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{extend}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(i) &=& \mathrm{signed}_N^{-1}(\mathrm{signed}_M(i)) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{wrap}_{M,N}(i)`

- Return `i` modulo `2^N`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{wrap}_{M,N}(i) &=& i \mathbin{\mathrm{mod}} 2^N \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then the result is undefined.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then the result is undefined.

- Else if `z` is a number and `\mathrm{trunc}(z)` is a value within range of the target type, then return that value.

- Else the result is undefined.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \{\} \\
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(\pm \infty) &=& \{\} \\
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{trunc}(\pm q) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} -1 < \mathrm{trunc}(\pm q) < 2^N) \\
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(\pm q) &=& \{\} & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

This operator is partial. It is not defined for NaNs, infinities, or values for which the result is out of range.

### `\mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then the result is undefined.

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then the result is undefined.

- If `z` is a number and `\mathrm{trunc}(z)` is a value within range of the target type, then return that value.

- Else the result is undefined.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \{\} \\
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(\pm \infty) &=& \{\} \\
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{trunc}(\pm q) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} -2^{N-1} - 1 < \mathrm{trunc}(\pm q) < 2^{N-1}) \\
    \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(\pm q) &=& \{\} & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

This operator is partial. It is not defined for NaNs, infinities, or values for which the result is out of range.

### `\mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}_{M,N}(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return `0`.

- Else if `z` is negative infinity, then return `0`.

- Else if `z` is positive infinity, then return `2^N - 1`.

- Else, return `\mathrm{sat\_u}_N(\mathrm{trunc}(z))`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}_{M,N}(- \infty) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}_{M,N}(+ \infty) &=& 2^N - 1 \\
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}_{M,N}(z) &=& \mathrm{sat\_u}_N(\mathrm{trunc}(z)) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}_{M,N}(z)`

- If `z` is a NaN, then return `0`.

- Else if `z` is negative infinity, then return `-2^{N-1}`.

- Else if `z` is positive infinity, then return `2^{N-1} - 1`.

- Else, return the value whose signed interpretation is `\mathrm{sat\_s}_N(\mathrm{trunc}(z))`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& 0 \\
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}_{M,N}(- \infty) &=& -2^{N-1} \\
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}_{M,N}(+ \infty) &=& 2^{N-1}-1 \\
    \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}_{M,N}(z) &=& \mathrm{signed}_N^{-1}(\mathrm{sat\_s}_N(\mathrm{trunc}(z))) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{promote}_{M,N}(z)`

- If `z` is a canonical NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{\}` (i.e., a canonical NaN of size `N`).

- Else if `z` is a NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(1)\}` (i.e., any arithmetic NaN of size `N`).

- Else, return `z`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{promote}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\} & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} n = \mathrm{canon}_N) \\
    \mathrm{promote}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{+ \mathsf{nan}(1)\} & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \mathrm{promote}_{M,N}(z) &=& z \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{demote}_{M,N}(z)`

- If `z` is a canonical NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{\}` (i.e., a canonical NaN of size `N`).

- Else if `z` is a NaN, then return an element of `\mathrm{nans}_N\{\pm \mathsf{nan}(1)\}` (i.e., any NaN of size `N`).

- Else if `z` is an infinity, then return that infinity.

- Else if `z` is a zero, then return that zero.

- Else, return `\mathrm{float}_N(z)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{demote}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{\} & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} n = \mathrm{canon}_N) \\
    \mathrm{demote}_{M,N}(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{nans}_N\{+ \mathsf{nan}(1)\} & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \mathrm{demote}_{M,N}(\pm \infty) &=& \pm \infty \\
    \mathrm{demote}_{M,N}(\pm 0) &=& \pm 0 \\
    \mathrm{demote}_{M,N}(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(\pm q) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{convert}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(i)`

- Return `\mathrm{float}_N(i)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{convert}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(i) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(i) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{convert}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(i)`

- Let `j` be the signed interpretation of `i`.

- Return `\mathrm{float}_N(j)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{convert}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(i) &=& \mathrm{float}_N(\mathrm{signed}_M(i)) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{reinterpret}_{t_1,t_2}(c)`

- Let `d^\ast` be the bit sequence `\mathrm{bits}_{t_1}(c)`.

- Return the constant `c'` for which `\mathrm{bits}_{t_2}(c') = d^\ast`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{reinterpret}_{t_1,t_2}(c) &=& \mathrm{bits}_{t_2}^{-1}(\mathrm{bits}_{t_1}(c)) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{narrow}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(i)`

- Let `j` be the signed interpretation of `i` of size `M`.

- Return the value whose signed interpretation is `\mathrm{sat\_s}_N(j)`.

    \begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{narrow}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(i) &=& \mathrm{signed}_N^{-1}(\mathrm{sat\_s}_N(\mathrm{signed}_M(i)))
    \end{array}

### `\mathrm{narrow}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(i)`

- Let `j` be the signed interpretation of `i` of size `M`.

- Return `\mathrm{sat\_u}_N(j)`.

    \begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathrm{narrow}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(i) &=& \mathrm{sat\_u}_N(\mathrm{signed}_M(i))
    \end{array}

## Vector Operations

Most vector operations are performed by applying numeric operations lanewise. However, some operators consider multiple lanes at once.

### `\mathrm{ivbitmask}_N(i^m)`

1.  For each `i_k` in `i^m`, let `b_k` be the result of computing `\mathrm{ilt\_s}_N(i, 0)`.

2.  Let `b^m` be the concatenation of all `b_k`.

3.  Return the result of computing `\mathrm{ibits}_{32}^{-1}((0)^{32-m}~b^m)`.

    \begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivbitmask}_N(i^m) &=& \mathrm{ibits}_{32}^{-1}((0)^{32-m}~\mathrm{ilt\_s}_{N}(i, 0)^m)
    \end{array}

### `\mathrm{ivswizzle}(i^n, j^n)`

1.  For each `j_k` in `j^n`, let `r_k` be the value `\mathrm{ivswizzle\_lane}(i^n, j_k)`.

2.  Let `r^n` be the concatenation of all `r_k`.

3.  Return `r^n`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcl}
    \mathrm{ivswizzle}(i^n, j^n) &=& \mathrm{ivswizzle\_lane}(i^n, j)^n \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

where:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivswizzle\_lane}(i^n, j) &=& i^n[j] & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} j < n) \\
    \mathrm{ivswizzle\_lane}(i^n, j) &=& 0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathrm{ivshuffle}(j^n, i_1^n, i_2^n)`

1.  Let `i^\ast` ne the concatenation of `i_1^n` and `i_2^n`.

2.  For each `j_k` in `j^n`, let `r_k` be `i^\ast[j_k]`.

3.  Let `r^n` be the concatenation of all `r_k`.

4.  Return `r^n`.

    \begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivshuffle}(j^n, i_1^n, i_2^n) &=& ((i_1^n~i_2^n)[j])^n
    & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} (j < 2\cdot n)^n)
    \end{array}

### `\mathrm{ivadd\_pairwise}_N(i^{2m})`

1.  Let `(i_1~i_2)^m` be `i^{2m}`, decomposed into pairwise elements.

2.  For each `i_{1k}` in `i_1^m` and corresponding `i_{2k}` in `i_2^m`, let `r_k` be `\mathrm{iadd}_N(i_{1k}, i_{2k})`.

3.  Let `r^m` be the concatenation of all `r_k`.

4.  Return `r^m`.

    \begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivadd\_pairwise}_N(i^{2m}) &=& (\mathrm{iadd}_N(i_1, i_2))^m
    & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} i^{2m} = (i_1~i_2)^m)
    \end{array}

### `\mathrm{ivmul}_N(i_1^m, i_2^m)`

1.  For each `i_{1k}` in `i_1^m` and corresponding `i_{2k}` in `i_2^m`, let `r_k` be `\mathrm{imul}_N(i_{1k}, i_{2k})`.

2.  Let `r^m` be the concatenation of all `r_k`.

3.  Return `r^m`.

    \begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivmul}_N(i_1^m, i_2^m) &=& (\mathrm{imul}_N(i_1, i_2))^m
    \end{array}

### `\mathrm{ivdot}_N(i_1^{2m}, i_2^{2m})`

1.  For each `i_{1k}` in `i_1^{2m}` and corresponding `i_{2k}` in `i_2^{2m}`, let `j_k` be `\mathrm{imul}_N(i_{1k}, i_{2k})`.

2.  Let `j^{2m}` be the concatenation of all `j_k`.

3.  Let `(j_1~j_2)^m` be `j^{2m}`, decomposed into pairwise elements.

4.  For each `i_{1k}` in `i_1^m` and corresponding `i_{2k}` in `i_2^m`, let `r_k` be `\mathrm{iadd}_N(i_{1k}, i_{2k})`.

5.  Let `r^m` be the concatenation of all `r_k`.

6.  Return `r^m`.

    \begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivdot}_N(i_1^{2m}, i_2^{2m}) &=& (\mathrm{iadd}_N(j_1, j_2))^m
    & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} (\mathrm{imul}_N(i_1, i_2))^{2m} = (j_1~j_2)^m)
    \end{array}

### `\mathrm{ivdotsat}_N(i_1^m, i_2^m)`

1.  For each `i_{1k}` in `i_1^{2m}` and corresponding `i_{2k}` in `i_2^{2m}`, let `j_k` be `\mathrm{imul}_N(i_{1k}, i_{2k})`.

2.  Let `j^{2m}` be the concatenation of all `j_k`.

3.  Let `(j_1~j_2)^m` be `j^{2m}`, decomposed into pairwise elements.

4.  For each `i_{1k}` in `i_1^m` and corresponding `i_{2k}` in `i_2^m`, let `r_k` be `\mathrm{iadd\_sat}_N(i_{1k}, i_{2k})`.

5.  Let `r^m` be the concatenation of all `r_k`.

6.  Return `r^m`.

    \begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivdotsat}_N(i_1^{2m}, i_2^{2m}) &=& (\mathrm{iadd\_sat}_N(j_1, j_2))^m
    & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} (\mathrm{imul}_N(i_1, i_2))^{2m} = (j_1~j_2)^m)
    \end{array}

The previous operators are lifted to operators on arguments of vector type by wrapping them in corresponding lane projections and injections and intermediate extension operations:

### `\mathit{vextunop}_{\mathit{sh}_1, \mathit{sh}_2}(c)`

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathsf{extadd\_pairwise}{\mathsf\_}\mathit{sx}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1, \mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(c) &=& \mathrm{lanes}^{-1}_{\mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(j^\ast)
    & (
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l}
    \mathrel{\mbox{if}} i^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1}(c) \\
    \land~{i'}^\ast = \mathrm{extend}^{\mathit{sx}}_{N_1, N_2}(i)^\ast \\
    \land~j^\ast = \mathrm{ivadd\_pairwise}_{N_2}({i'}^\ast) \\
    \end{array}
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathit{vextbinop}_{\mathit{sh}_1, \mathit{sh}_2}(c_1, c_2)`

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathit{vextbinop}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1, \mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(c_1, c_2) &=& \mathrm{lanes}^{-1}_{\mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(j^\ast)
    & (
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l}
    \mathrel{\mbox{if}} i_1^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1}(c_1)[h \mathrel{\mathbf{:}} k] \\
    \land~i_2^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1}(c_2)[h \mathrel{\mathbf{:}} k] \\
    \land~{i'_1}^\ast = \mathrm{extend}^{\mathit{sx}}_{N_1, N_2}(i_1)^\ast \\
    \land~{i'_2}^\ast = \mathrm{extend}^{\mathit{sx}}_{N_1, N_2}(i_2)^\ast \\
    \land~j^\ast = f_{N_2}({i'_1}^\ast, {i'_2}^\ast) \\
    \end{array}
    \end{array}\end{split}

where `f`, `\mathit{sx}_1`, `\mathit{sx}_2`, `h`, and `k` are instantiated as follows, depending on the operator:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}l|lllll}
    \mathit{vextbinop} & f & \mathit{sx}_1 & \mathit{sx}_2 & h & k \\
    \hline
    \mathsf{extmul}{\mathsf\_}\mathsf{low}{\mathsf\_}\mathit{sx} & \mathrm{ivmul} & \mathit{sx} & \mathit{sx} & 0 & M_2 \\
    \mathsf{extmul}{\mathsf\_}\mathsf{high}{\mathsf\_}\mathit{sx} & \mathrm{ivmul} & \mathit{sx} & \mathit{sx} & M_2 & M_2 \\
    \mathsf{dot}{\mathsf\_}\mathsf{s} & \mathrm{ivdot} & \mathsf{s} & \mathsf{s} & 0 & M_1 \\
    \mathsf{relaxed\_dot}{\mathsf\_}\mathsf{s} & \mathrm{ivdotsat} & \mathsf{s} & \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{idot}})[ \mathsf{s}, \mathsf{u} ] & 0 & M_1 \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed operations and the paramater `R_{\mathrm{idot}}` are introduced below.

### `\mathit{vextternop}_{\mathit{sh}_1, \mathit{sh}_2}(c_1, c_2, c_3)`

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathsf{relaxed\_dot\_add}{\mathsf\_}\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1, \mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(c_1, c_2, c_3) &=& c
    & (
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l}
    \mathrel{\mbox{if}} N = 2\cdot N_1 \\
    \land~M = 2\cdot M_2 \\
    \land~c' = \mathsf{relaxed\_dot}{\mathsf\_}\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1, \mathsf{i}N\mathsf{x}M}(c_1, c_2) \\
    \land~c'' = \mathsf{extadd\_pairwise}{\mathsf\_}\mathsf{s}_{\mathsf{i}N\mathsf{x}M, \mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(c') \\
    \land~c \in \mathsf{add}_{\mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(c'', c_3) \\
    \end{array}
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{narrow}{\mathsf\_}\mathit{sx}_{\mathit{sh}_1, \mathit{sh}_2}(c_1, c_2)`

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathsf{narrow}{\mathsf\_}\mathit{sx}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1, \mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(c_1, c_2) &=& \mathrm{lanes}^{-1}_{\mathsf{i}N_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(j^\ast)
    & (
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l}
    \mathrel{\mbox{if}} i_1^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1}(c_1) \\
    \land~i_2^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{\mathsf{i}N_1\mathsf{x}M_1}(c_2) \\
    \land~{i'_1}^\ast = \mathrm{narrow}^{\mathit{sx}}_{N_1, N_2}(i_1)^\ast \\
    \land~{i'_2}^\ast = \mathrm{narrow}^{\mathit{sx}}_{N_1, N_2}(i_2)^\ast \\
    \land~j^\ast = {i'_1}^\ast \oplus {i'_1}^\ast \\
    \end{array}
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathit{vcvtop}{\mathsf\_}\mathit{half}^?{\mathsf\_}\mathit{zero}^?_{\mathit{sh}_1, \mathit{sh}_2}(i)`

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathit{vcvtop}{\mathsf\_}\mathit{half}^?{\mathsf\_}\mathit{zero}^?_{t_1\mathsf{x}M_1, t_2\mathsf{x}M_2}(i) &=& j
    & (
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l}
    \mathrel{\mbox{if}} \mathit{condition} \\
    \land~c^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{t_1\mathsf{x}M_1}(i)[h \mathrel{\mathbf{:}} k] \\
    \land~{{c'}^\ast}^\ast = \Large\times (\mathit{vcvtop}_{|t_1|, |t_2|}(c)^\ast \oplus (0)^n) \\
    \land~j \in \mathrm{lanes}^{-1}_{t_2\mathsf{x}M_2}({c'}^\ast)^\ast \\
    \end{array}
    \end{array}\end{split}

where `h`, `k`, `n`, and `\mathit{condition}` are instantiated as follows, depending on the operator:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}ll|llllll}
    \mathit{half}^?  & \mathit{zero}^?  & h   & k   & n   & \mathit{condition} \\
    \hline
    \epsilon & \epsilon & 0   & M_1 & 0   & (M_1 = M_2) \\
    \mathsf{low}     & \epsilon & 0   & M_2 & 0   & (M_1 = 2\cdot M_2) \\
    \mathsf{high}    & \epsilon & M_2 & M_2 & 0   & (M_1 = 2\cdot M_2) \\
    \epsilon & \mathsf{zero}    & 0   & M_1 & M_1 & (2\cdot M_1 = M_2) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

while `\Large\times \{x^\ast\}^N` transforms a sequence of `N` sets of non-deterministic values into a set of non-deterministic sequences of `N` values by computing the set product:

    \begin{array}{lll}
    \Large\times (S_1 \dots S_N) &=& \{ x_1 \dots x_N ~|~ x_1 \in S_1 \land \dots \land x_N \in S_N \}
    \end{array}

## Relaxed Operations

The result of *relaxed* operators are *implementation-dependent*, because the set of possible results may depend on properties of the host environment, such as its hardware. Technically, their behaviour is controlled by a set of *global parameters* to the semantics that an implementation can instantiate in different ways. These choices are fixed, that is, parameters are constant during the execution of any given program.

Every such parameter is an index into a sequence of possible sets of results and must be instantiated to a defined index. In the deterministic profile, every parameter is prescribed to be 0. This behaviour is expressed by the following auxiliary function, where `R` is a global parameter selecting one of the allowed outcomes:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \def\mathdef1803#1{{{}^{\small{[{!}#1]}}}}\mathdef1803{\mathrm{DET}} & \mathrm{relaxed}(R)[ A_0, \dots, A_n ] = A_R \\
    & \mathrm{relaxed}(R)[ A_0, \dots, A_n ] = A_0 \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Each parameter can be thought of as inducing a family of operations that is fixed to one particular choice by an implementation. The fixed operation itself can still be non-deterministic or partial.

Implementations are expexted to either choose the behaviour that is the most efficient on the underlying hardware, or the behaviour of the deterministic profile.

### `\mathrm{frelaxed\_madd}_N(z_1, z_2, z_3)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{fmadd}} \in \{0, 1\}`.

- Return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmadd}})[\mathrm{fadd}_N(\mathrm{fmul}_N(z_1, z_2), z_3), \mathrm{fma}_N(z_1, z_2, z_3)]`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_madd}_N(z_1, z_2, z_3) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmadd}})[ \mathrm{fadd}_N(\mathrm{fmul}_N(z_1, z_2), z_3), \mathrm{fma}_N(z_1, z_2, z_3) ] \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed multiply-add allows for fused or unfused results, which leads to implementation-dependent rounding behaviour. In the deterministic profile, the unfused behaviour is used.

### `\mathrm{frelaxed\_nmadd}_N(z_1, z_2, z_3)`

- Return `\mathrm{frelaxed\_madd}(-z_1, z_2, z_3)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_nmadd}_N(z_1, z_2, z_3) &=& \mathrm{frelaxed\_madd}_N(-z_1, z_2, z_3) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

This operation is implementation-dependent because `\mathrm{frelaxed\_madd}` is implementation-dependent.

### `\mathrm{frelaxed\_min}_N(z_1, z_2)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{fmin}} \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}`.

- If `z_1` is a NaN, then return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmin}})[ \mathrm{fmin}_N(z_1, z_2), \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2, z_2 ]`.

- If `z_2` is a NaN, then return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmin}})[ \mathrm{fmin}_N(z_1, z_2), z_1, \mathsf{nan}(n), z_1 ]`.

- If both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes of opposite sign, then return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmin}})[ \mathrm{fmin}_N(z_1, z_2)`, pm 0, mp 0, -0 \]\`.

- Return `\mathrm{fmin}_N(z_1, z_2)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_min}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmin}})[ \mathrm{fmin}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2), \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2, z_2 ] \\
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_min}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmin}})[ \mathrm{fmin}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)), z_1, \mathsf{nan}(n), z_1 ] \\
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_min}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmin}})[ \mathrm{fmin}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0), \pm 0, \mp 0, -0 ] \\
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_min}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{fmin}_N(z_1, z_2) & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed minimum is implementation-dependent for NaNs and for zeroes with different signs. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like regular `\mathrm{fmin}`.

### `\mathrm{frelaxed\_max}_N(z_1, z_2)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{fmax}} \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}`.

- If `z_1` is a NaN, then return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmax}})[ \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, z_2), \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2, z_2 ]`.

- If `z_2` is a NaN, then return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmax}})[ \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, z_2), z_1, \mathsf{nan}(n), z_1 ]`.

- If both `z_1` and `z_2` are zeroes of opposite sign, then return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmax}})[ \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, z_2)`, pm 0, mp 0, +0 \]\`.

- Return `\mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, z_2)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_max}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmax}})[ \mathrm{fmax}_N(\pm \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2), \mathsf{nan}(n), z_2, z_2 ] \\
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_max}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmax}})[ \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, \pm \mathsf{nan}(n)), z_1, \mathsf{nan}(n), z_1 ] \\
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_max}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{fmax}})[ \mathrm{fmax}_N(\pm 0, \mp 0), \pm 0, \mp 0, +0 ] \\
    \mathrm{frelaxed\_max}_N(z_1, z_2) &=& \mathrm{fmax}_N(z_1, z_2) & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed maximum is implementation-dependent for NaNs and for zeroes with different signs. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like regular `\mathrm{fmax}`.

### `\mathrm{irelaxed\_q15mulr\_s}_N(i_1, i_2)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{iq15mulr}} \in \{0, 1\}`.

- If both `i_1` and `i_2` equal `(\mathrm{signed}^{-1}_N(-2^{N-1})`, then return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{iq15mulr}})[ 2^{N-1}-1, \mathrm{signed}^{-1}_N(-2^{N-1}) ]`.

- Return `\mathrm{iq15mulrsat\_s}(i_1, i_2)`

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{irelaxed\_q15mulr\_s}_N(\mathrm{signed}^{-1}_N(-2^{N-1}), \mathrm{signed}^{-1}_N(-2^{N-1})) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{iq15mulr}})[ 2^{N-1}-1, \mathrm{signed}^{-1}_N(-2^{N-1}) ] & \\
    \mathrm{irelaxed\_q15mulr\_s}_N(i_1, i_2) &=& \mathrm{iq15mulrsat\_s}(i_1, i_2)
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed Q15 multiplication is implementation-dependent when the result overflows. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like regular `\mathrm{iq15mulrsat\_s}`.

### `\mathrm{relaxed\_trunc}^u_{M,N}(z)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{trunc\_u}} \in \{0, 1\}`.

- If `z` is normal or subnormal and `\mathrm{trunc}(z)` is non-negative and less than `2^N`, then return `\mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(z)`.

- Else, return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{trunc\_u}})[ \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}_{M,N}(z), \mathbf{R} ]`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{relaxed\_trunc}^u_{M,N}(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{u}}_{M,N}(\pm q) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} 0 \leq \mathrm{trunc}(\pm q) < 2^N) \\
    \mathrm{relaxed\_trunc}^u_{M,N}(z) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{trunc\_u}})[ \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}_{M,N}(z), \mathbf{R}] & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed unsigned truncation is non-deterministic for NaNs and out-of-range values. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like regular `\mathrm{trunc\_sat\_u}`.

### `\mathrm{relaxed\_trunc}^s_{M,N}(z)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{trunc\_s}} \in \{0, 1\}`.

- If `z` is normal or subnormal and `\mathrm{trunc}(z)` is greater than or equal to `-2^{N-1}` and less than `2^{N-1}`, then return `\mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(z)`.

- Else, return `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{trunc\_s}})[ \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}_{M,N}(z), \mathbf{R} ]`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{relaxed\_trunc}^s_{M,N}(\pm q) &=& \mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{M,N}(\pm q) & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} -2^{N-1} \leq \mathrm{trunc}(\pm q) < 2^{N-1}) \\
    \mathrm{relaxed\_trunc}^s_{M,N}(z) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{trunc\_s}})[ \mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}_{M,N}(z), \mathbf{R}] & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed signed truncation is non-deterministic for NaNs and out-of-range values. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like regular `\mathrm{trunc\_sat\_s}`.

### `\mathrm{ivrelaxed\_swizzle}(i^n, j^n)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{swizzle}} \in \{0, 1\}`.

- For each `j_k` in `j^n`, let `r_k` be the value `\mathrm{ivrelaxed\_swizzle\_lane}(i^n, j_k)`.

- Let `r^n` be the concatenation of all `r_k`.

- Return `r^n`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcl}
    \mathrm{ivrelaxed\_swizzle}(i^n, j^n) &=& \mathrm{ivrelaxed\_swizzle\_lane}(i^n, j)^n \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

where:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{ivrelaxed\_swizzle\_lane}(i^n, j) &=& i[j] & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} j < 16) \\
    \mathrm{ivrelaxed\_swizzle\_lane}(i^n, j) &=& 0 & (\mathrel{\mbox{if}} \mathrm{signed}_8(j) < 0) \\
    \mathrm{ivrelaxed\_swizzle\_lane}(i^n, j) &=& \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{swizzle}})[ 0, i^n[j \mathbin{\mathrm{mod}} n] ] & (\mathrel{\mbox{otherwise}}) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed swizzle is implementation-dependent if the signed interpretation of any of the 8-bit indices in `j^n` is larger than or equal to 16. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like regular `\mathrm{ivswizzle}`.

### `\mathsf{relaxed\_dot}(i_1, i_2)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{idot}} \in \{0, 1\}`. It also affects the behaviour of `\mathsf{relaxed\_dot\_add}`.

Its definition is part of the definition of `\mathit{vextbinop}` specified above.

Note

Relaxed dot product is implementation-dependent when the second operand is negative in a signed intepretation. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like signed dot product.

### `\mathrm{irelaxed\_laneselect}_N(i_1, i_2, i_3)`

The implementation-specific behaviour of this operation is determined by the global parameter `R_{\mathrm{laneselect}} \in \{0, 1\}`.

- If `i_3` is smaller than `2^{N-1}`, then let `i'_3` be the value `0`, otherwise `2^N-1`.

- Let `i''_3` be `\mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{laneselect}})[i_3, i'_3]`.

- Return `\mathrm{ibitselect}_N(i_1, i_2, i''_3)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{@{}lcll}
    \mathrm{irelaxed\_laneselect}_N(i_1, i_2, i_3) &=& \mathrm{ibitselect}_N(i_1, i_2, \mathrm{relaxed}(R_{\mathrm{laneselect}})[ i_3, \mathrm{extend}^{\mathsf{s}}_{1,N}(\mathrm{ishr\_u}_N(i_3, N-1)) ]) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Relaxed lane selection is non-deterministic when the mask mixes set and cleared bits, since the value of the high bit may or may not be expanded to all bits. In the deterministic profile, it behaves like `\mathrm{ibitselect}`.

# Types

Execution has to check and compare types in a few places, such as executing `\mathsf{call\_indirect}` or instantiating modules.

It is an invariant of the semantics that all types occurring during execution are closed.

Note

Runtime type checks generally involve types from multiple modules or types not defined by a module at all, such that any module-local type indices occurring inside them would not generally be meaningful.

## Instantiation

Any form of type can be *instantiated* into a closed type inside a module instance by substituting each type index `x` occurring in it with the corresponding defined type `{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {{\mathrm{clos}}}_{{\mathit{moduleinst}}}(t) & = & {t}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{types} ]} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

This is the runtime equivalent to type closure, which is applied at validation time.

# Values

## Value Typing

For the purpose of checking argument values against the parameter types of exported functions, values are classified by value types. The following auxiliary typing rules specify this typing relation relative to a store `S` in which possibly referenced addresses live.

### Numeric Values

The number value `({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` is valid with the number type `{\mathit{nt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    s \vdash {\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c : {\mathit{nt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Vector Values

The vector value `({\mathit{vt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` is valid with the vector type `{\mathit{vt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    s \vdash {\mathit{vt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c : {\mathit{vt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Null References

The reference value `\mathsf{ref{.}null}` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{bot})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}null} : \mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~\mathsf{bot}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Scalar References

The reference value `(\mathsf{ref{.}i\scriptstyle31}~i)` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle31})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}i\scriptstyle31}~i : \mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{i\scriptstyle31}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Structure References

The reference value `(\mathsf{ref{.}struct}~a)` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}})` if:

> - The structure instance `s{.}\mathsf{structs}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The defined type `s{.}\mathsf{structs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type}` is of the form `{\mathit{dt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{structs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type} = {\mathit{dt}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}struct}~a : \mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Array References

The reference value `(\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}})` if:

> - The array instance `s{.}\mathsf{arrays}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The defined type `s{.}\mathsf{arrays}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type}` is of the form `{\mathit{dt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{arrays}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type} = {\mathit{dt}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}array}~a : \mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Exception References

The reference value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{exn})` if:

> - The exception instance `s{.}\mathsf{exns}{}[a]` exists.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{exns}{}[a] = {\mathit{exn}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a : \mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{exn}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Function References

The reference value `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}})` if:

> - The function instance `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The defined type `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type}` is of the form `{\mathit{dt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type} = {\mathit{dt}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}func}~a : \mathsf{ref}~{\mathit{dt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Host References

The reference value `(\mathsf{ref{.}host}~a)` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{any})`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}host}~a : \mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{any}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

Note

A bare host reference is considered internalized.

### External References

The reference value `(\mathsf{ref{.}extern}~{\mathit{ref}})` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{extern})` if:

> - The reference value `{\mathit{ref}}` is valid with the reference type `(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{any})`.
>
> - The reference value `{\mathit{ref}}` is not of the form `\mathsf{ref{.}null}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s \vdash {\mathit{ref}} : \mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{any}
    \qquad
    {\mathit{ref}} \neq \mathsf{ref{.}null}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{ref{.}extern}~{\mathit{ref}} : \mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{extern}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Subsumption

The reference value `{\mathit{ref}}` is valid with the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` if:

> - The reference value `{\mathit{ref}}` is valid with the reference type `{\mathit{rt}'}`.
>
> - Under the context `\{ \mathsf{return}~\epsilon \}`, the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}` is valid.
>
> - The reference type `{\mathit{rt}'}` matches the reference type `{\mathit{rt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s \vdash {\mathit{ref}} : {\mathit{rt}'}
    \qquad
    \{  \} \vdash {\mathit{rt}} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    \{  \} \vdash {\mathit{rt}'} \leq {\mathit{rt}}
    }{
    s \vdash {\mathit{ref}} : {\mathit{rt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

## External Typing

For the purpose of checking external address against imports, such values are classified by external types. The following auxiliary typing rules specify this typing relation relative to a store `S` in which the referenced instances live.

### Functions

The external address `(\mathsf{func}~a)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{funcinst}}{.}\mathsf{type})` if:

> - The function instance `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The function instance `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]` is of the form `{\mathit{funcinst}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a] = {\mathit{funcinst}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{func}~a : \mathsf{func}~{\mathit{funcinst}}{.}\mathsf{type}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Tables

The external address `(\mathsf{table}~a)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tableinst}}{.}\mathsf{type})` if:

> - The table instance `s{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The table instance `s{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[a]` is of the form `{\mathit{tableinst}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[a] = {\mathit{tableinst}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{table}~a : \mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tableinst}}{.}\mathsf{type}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Memories

The external address `(\mathsf{mem}~a)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{mem}~{\mathit{meminst}}{.}\mathsf{type})` if:

> - The memory instance `s{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The memory instance `s{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[a]` is of the form `{\mathit{meminst}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[a] = {\mathit{meminst}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{mem}~a : \mathsf{mem}~{\mathit{meminst}}{.}\mathsf{type}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Globals

The external address `(\mathsf{global}~a)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globalinst}}{.}\mathsf{type})` if:

> - The global instance `s{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The global instance `s{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[a]` is of the form `{\mathit{globalinst}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[a] = {\mathit{globalinst}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{global}~a : \mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globalinst}}{.}\mathsf{type}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Tags

The external address `(\mathsf{tag}~a)` is valid with the external type `(\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{taginst}}{.}\mathsf{type})` if:

> - The tag instance `s{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[a]` exists.
>
> - The tag instance `s{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[a]` is of the form `{\mathit{taginst}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[a] = {\mathit{taginst}}
    }{
    s \vdash \mathsf{tag}~a : \mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{taginst}}{.}\mathsf{type}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

### Subsumption

The external address `{\mathit{externaddr}}` is valid with the external type `{\mathit{xt}}` if:

> - The external address `{\mathit{externaddr}}` is valid with the external type `{\mathit{xt}'}`.
>
> - Under the context `\{ \mathsf{return}~\epsilon \}`, the external type `{\mathit{xt}}` is valid.
>
> - The external type `{\mathit{xt}'}` matches the external type `{\mathit{xt}}`.

    \begin{array}{@{}c@{}}\displaystyle
    \frac{
    s \vdash {\mathit{externaddr}} : {\mathit{xt}'}
    \qquad
    \{  \} \vdash {\mathit{xt}} : \mathsf{ok}
    \qquad
    \{  \} \vdash {\mathit{xt}'} \leq {\mathit{xt}}
    }{
    s \vdash {\mathit{externaddr}} : {\mathit{xt}}
    }
    \qquad
    \end{array}

# Instructions

WebAssembly computation is performed by executing individual instructions.

## Parametric Instructions

### `\mathsf{nop}`

1.  Do nothing.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & \mathsf{nop} & \hookrightarrow & \epsilon \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{unreachable}`

1.  Trap.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & \mathsf{unreachable} & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{drop}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}}` from the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathit{val}}~\mathsf{drop} & \hookrightarrow & \epsilon \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{select}~{({t^\ast})^?}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

4.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}}_2` from the stack.

5.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

6.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}}_1` from the stack.

7.  If `c \neq 0`, then:

    1.  Push the value `{\mathit{val}}_1` to the stack.

8.  Else:

    1.  Push the value `{\mathit{val}}_2` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathit{val}}_1~{\mathit{val}}_2~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)~(\mathsf{select}~{({t^\ast})^?}) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{val}}_1 & \quad \mbox{if}~ c \neq 0 \\
    & {\mathit{val}}_1~{\mathit{val}}_2~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)~(\mathsf{select}~{({t^\ast})^?}) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{val}}_2 & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = 0 \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

In future versions of WebAssembly, `\mathsf{select}` may allow more than one value per choice.

## Control Instructions

### `\mathsf{block}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Let `{t_1^{m}}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{{\mathit{localidx}}_0^\ast}}\,{t_2^{n}}` be the destructuring of `{{\mathrm{instrtype}}}_{z}({\mathit{bt}})`.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, `{{\mathit{localidx}}_0^\ast} = \epsilon`.

4.  Assert: Due to validation, there are at least `m` values on the top of the stack.

5.  Pop the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{m}}` from the stack.

6.  Let `L` be the `\mathsf{label}` whose arity is `n` and whose continuation is the end of the block.

7.  Enter the block `{{\mathit{val}}^{m}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` with the `\mathsf{label}` `L`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; {{\mathit{val}}^{m}}~(\mathsf{block}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & ({{\mathsf{label}}_{n}}{\{ \epsilon \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^{m}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathrm{instrtype}}}_{z}({\mathit{bt}}) = {t_1^{m}} \rightarrow {t_2^{n}} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{loop}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Let `{t_1^{m}}~{\mathrel{\rightarrow}}_{{{\mathit{localidx}}_0^\ast}}\,{t_2^{n}}` be the destructuring of `{{\mathrm{instrtype}}}_{z}({\mathit{bt}})`.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, `{{\mathit{localidx}}_0^\ast} = \epsilon`.

4.  Assert: Due to validation, there are at least `m` values on the top of the stack.

5.  Pop the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{m}}` from the stack.

6.  Let `L` be the `\mathsf{label}` whose arity is `m` and whose continuation is the start of the block.

7.  Enter the block `{{\mathit{val}}^{m}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}` with the `\mathsf{label}` `L`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; {{\mathit{val}}^{m}}~(\mathsf{loop}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & ({{\mathsf{label}}_{m}}{\{ \mathsf{loop}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^{m}}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathrm{instrtype}}}_{z}({\mathit{bt}}) = {t_1^{m}} \rightarrow {t_2^{n}} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{if}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}~\mathsf{else}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` from the stack.

3.  If `c \neq 0`, then:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{block}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast})`.

4.  Else:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{block}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast})`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)~(\mathsf{if}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}~\mathsf{else}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{block}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c \neq 0 \\
    & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)~(\mathsf{if}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_1^\ast}~\mathsf{else}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{block}~{\mathit{bt}}~{{\mathit{instr}}_2^\ast}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = 0 \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{br}~l`

1.  If the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{label}`, then:

    1.  Let `L` be the topmost `\mathsf{label}`.

    2.  Let `n` be the arity of `L`

    3.  If `l = 0`, then:

        1.  Assert: Due to validation, there are at least `n` values on the top of the stack.

        2.  Pop the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}` from the stack.

        3.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

        4.  Pop the `\mathsf{label}` from the stack.

        5.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}` to the stack.

        6.  Jump to the continuation of `L`.

    4.  Else:

        1.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

        2.  Pop the `\mathsf{label}` from the stack.

        3.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

        4.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l - 1)`.

2.  Else:

    1.  Assert: Due to validation, the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{handler}`.

    2.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    3.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

    4.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

    5.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & ({{\mathsf{label}}_{n}}{\{ {{\mathit{instr}'}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}~{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}~(\mathsf{br}~l)~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^{n}}~{{\mathit{instr}'}^\ast} & \quad \mbox{if}~ l = 0 \\
    & ({{\mathsf{label}}_{n}}{\{ {{\mathit{instr}'}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{br}~l)~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{br}~l - 1) & \quad \mbox{if}~ l > 0 \\
    & ({{\mathsf{handler}}_{n}}{\{ {{\mathit{catch}}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{br}~l)~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{br}~l) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{br\_if}~l`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` from the stack.

3.  If `c \neq 0`, then:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

4.  Else:

    1.  Do nothing.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)~(\mathsf{br\_if}~l) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{br}~l) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c \neq 0 \\
    & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)~(\mathsf{br\_if}~l) & \hookrightarrow & \epsilon & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = 0 \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{br\_table}~{l^\ast}~{l'}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)` from the stack.

3.  If `i < {|{l^\ast}|}`, then:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~{l^\ast}{}[i])`.

4.  Else:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~{l'})`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{br\_table}~{l^\ast}~{l'}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{br}~{l^\ast}{}[i]) & \quad \mbox{if}~ i < {|{l^\ast}|} \\
    & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{br\_table}~{l^\ast}~{l'}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{br}~{l'}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ i \geq {|{l^\ast}|} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_null}~l`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}}` from the stack.

3.  If `{\mathit{val}} = \mathsf{ref{.}null}`, then:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

4.  Else:

    1.  Push the value `{\mathit{val}}` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathit{val}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_null}~l) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{br}~l) & \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{val}} = \mathsf{ref{.}null} \\
    & {\mathit{val}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_null}~l) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{val}} & \quad \mbox{otherwise} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_non\_null}~l`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}}` from the stack.

3.  If `{\mathit{val}} = \mathsf{ref{.}null}`, then:

    1.  Do nothing.

4.  Else:

    1.  Push the value `{\mathit{val}}` to the stack.

    2.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathit{val}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_non\_null}~l) & \hookrightarrow & \epsilon & \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{val}} = \mathsf{ref{.}null} \\
    & {\mathit{val}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_non\_null}~l) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{val}}~(\mathsf{br}~l) & \quad \mbox{otherwise} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_cast}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2`

1.  Let `f` be the topmost `\mathsf{frame}`.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, a reference value is on the top of the stack.

3.  Pop the value `{\mathit{ref}}` from the stack.

4.  Push the value `{\mathit{ref}}` to the stack.

5.  If `{\mathit{ref}}` is valid with type `{{\mathrm{clos}}}_{f{.}\mathsf{module}}({\mathit{rt}}_2)`, then:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

6.  Else:

    1.  Do nothing.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & s ; f ; {\mathit{ref}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_cast}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{ref}}~(\mathsf{br}~l) & \quad \mbox{if}~ s \vdash {\mathit{ref}} : {{\mathrm{clos}}}_{f{.}\mathsf{module}}({\mathit{rt}}_2) \\
    & s ; f ; {\mathit{ref}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_cast}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{ref}} & \quad \mbox{otherwise} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{br\_on\_cast\_fail}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2`

1.  Let `f` be the topmost `\mathsf{frame}`.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, a reference value is on the top of the stack.

3.  Pop the value `{\mathit{ref}}` from the stack.

4.  Push the value `{\mathit{ref}}` to the stack.

5.  If `{\mathit{ref}}` is valid with type `{{\mathrm{clos}}}_{f{.}\mathsf{module}}({\mathit{rt}}_2)`, then:

    1.  Do nothing.

6.  Else:

    1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & s ; f ; {\mathit{ref}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_cast\_fail}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{ref}} & \quad \mbox{if}~ s \vdash {\mathit{ref}} : {{\mathrm{clos}}}_{f{.}\mathsf{module}}({\mathit{rt}}_2) \\
    & s ; f ; {\mathit{ref}}~(\mathsf{br\_on\_cast\_fail}~l~{\mathit{rt}}_1~{\mathit{rt}}_2) & \hookrightarrow & {\mathit{ref}}~(\mathsf{br}~l) & \quad \mbox{otherwise} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{return}`

1.  If the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{frame}`, then:

    1.  Let `f` be the topmost `\mathsf{frame}`.

    2.  Let `n` be the arity of `f`

    3.  Assert: Due to validation, there are at least `n` values on the top of the stack.

    4.  Pop the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}` from the stack.

    5.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    6.  Pop the `\mathsf{frame}` from the stack.

    7.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}` to the stack.

2.  Else if the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{label}`, then:

    1.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    2.  Pop the `\mathsf{label}` from the stack.

    3.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

    4.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{return}`.

3.  Else:

    1.  Assert: Due to validation, the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{handler}`.

    2.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    3.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

    4.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

    5.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{return}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & ({{\mathsf{frame}}_{n}}{\{ f \}}~{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}~{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}~\mathsf{return}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^{n}} \\
    & ({{\mathsf{label}}_{n}}{\{ {{\mathit{instr}'}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~\mathsf{return}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~\mathsf{return} \\
    & ({{\mathsf{handler}}_{n}}{\{ {{\mathit{catch}}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~\mathsf{return}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~\mathsf{return} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{call}~x`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, `x < {|z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{funcs}|}`.

3.  Let `a` be the address `z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]`.

4.  Assert: Due to validation, `a < {|z{.}\mathsf{funcs}|}`.

5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)` to the stack.

6.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{call\_ref}~z{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type})`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; (\mathsf{call}~x) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)~(\mathsf{call\_ref}~z{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x] = a \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{call\_ref}~x`

Todo

(\*) Prose not spliced, for the prose merges the two cases of null and non-null references.

1.  Assert: due to validation, a null or function reference is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the reference value `r` from the stack.

3.  If `r` is `\mathsf{ref{.}null}~\mathit{ht}`, then:

    > 1.  Trap.

4.  Assert: due to validation, `r` is a function reference.

5.  Let `\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a` be the reference `r`.

6.  Invoke the function instance at address `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}null})~(\mathsf{call\_ref}~y) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

The formal rule for calling a non-null function reference is described below.

### `\mathsf{call\_indirect}~x~y`

1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}get}~x)`.

2.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{ref{.}cast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~y))`.

3.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{call\_ref}~y)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{call\_indirect}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{table{.}get}~x)~(\mathsf{ref{.}cast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~y))~(\mathsf{call\_ref}~y) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{return\_call}~x`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, `x < {|z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{funcs}|}`.

3.  Let `a` be the address `z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]`.

4.  Assert: Due to validation, `a < {|z{.}\mathsf{funcs}|}`.

5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)` to the stack.

6.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~z{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type})`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; (\mathsf{return\_call}~x) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~z{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x] = a \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  If the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{label}`, then:

    1.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    2.  Pop the `\mathsf{label}` from the stack.

    3.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

    4.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y)`.

3.  Else if the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{handler}`, then:

    1.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

    3.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

    4.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y)`.

4.  Else:

    1.  Assert: Due to validation, the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{frame}`.

    2.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

    3.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}''}` from the stack.

    4.  If `{\mathit{val}''} = \mathsf{ref{.}null}`, then:

        1.  Trap.

    5.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{val}''}` is some `\mathsf{ref{.}func}~{\mathit{funcaddr}}`.

    6.  Let `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{val}''}`.

    7.  Assert: Due to validation, `a < {|z{.}\mathsf{funcs}|}`.

    8.  Assert: Due to validation, the expansion of `z{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type}` is some `\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{resulttype}} \rightarrow {\mathit{resulttype}}`.

    9.  Let `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^{n}}~\rightarrow~{t_2^{m}})` be the destructuring of the expansion of `z{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type}`.

    10. Assert: Due to validation, there are at least `n` values on the top of the stack.

    11. Pop the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}` from the stack.

    12. Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    13. Pop the `\mathsf{frame}` from the stack.

    14. Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}` to the stack.

    15. Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)` to the stack.

    16. Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{call\_ref}~y)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{label}}_{k}}{\{ {{\mathit{instr}'}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y)~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y) \\
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{handler}}_{k}}{\{ {{\mathit{catch}}^\ast} \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y)~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y) \\
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{frame}}_{k}}{\{ f \}}~{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref{.}null})~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y)~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} \\
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{frame}}_{k}}{\{ f \}}~{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}~{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}~(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y)~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^{n}}~(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~a)~(\mathsf{call\_ref}~y) &  \\
    &&& \multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ z{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{type} \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^{n}} \rightarrow {t_2^{m}}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{return\_call\_indirect}~x~y`

1.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{table{.}get}~x)`.

2.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{ref{.}cast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~y))`.

3.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{return\_call\_indirect}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{table{.}get}~x)~(\mathsf{ref{.}cast}~(\mathsf{ref}~\mathsf{null}~y))~(\mathsf{return\_call\_ref}~y) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{throw}~x`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, `x < {|z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}|}`.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, the expansion of `z{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]{.}\mathsf{type}` is some `\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{resulttype}} \rightarrow {\mathit{resulttype}}`.

4.  Let `(\mathsf{func}~{t^{n}}~\rightarrow~{\mathit{resulttype}}_0)` be the destructuring of the expansion of `z{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]{.}\mathsf{type}`.

5.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{resulttype}}_0 = \epsilon`.

6.  Let `a` be the length of `z{.}\mathsf{exns}`.

7.  Assert: Due to validation, there are at least `n` values on the top of the stack.

8.  Pop the values `{{\mathit{val}}^{n}}` from the stack.

9.  Let `{\mathit{exn}}` be the exception instance `\{ \mathsf{tag}~z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x],\;\allowbreak \mathsf{fields}~{{\mathit{val}}^{n}} \}`.

10. Append `{\mathit{exn}}` to `z{.}\mathsf{exns}`.

11. Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

12. Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; {{\mathit{val}}^{n}}~(\mathsf{throw}~x) & \hookrightarrow & z{}[{.}\mathsf{exns} \mathrel{{=}{\oplus}} {\mathit{exn}}] ; (\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref} & \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ z{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]{.}\mathsf{type} \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t^{n}} \rightarrow \epsilon \\
    {\land}~ a = {|z{.}\mathsf{exns}|} \\
    {\land}~ {\mathit{exn}} = \{ \mathsf{tag}~z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x],\;\allowbreak \mathsf{fields}~{{\mathit{val}}^{n}} \} \\
    \end{array} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

3.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}'}` from the stack.

4.  If `{\mathit{val}'} = \mathsf{ref{.}null}`, then:

    1.  Trap.

5.  If `{\mathit{val}'}` is some `\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~{\mathit{exnaddr}}`, then:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{val}'}`.

    2.  Pop all values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` from the top of the stack.

    3.  If `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast} \neq \epsilon`, then:

        1.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

        2.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

    4.  Else if the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{label}`, then:

        1.  Pop the `\mathsf{label}` from the stack.

        2.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

        3.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

    5.  Else:

        1.  If the first non-value entry of the stack is a `\mathsf{frame}`, then:

            1.  Pop the `\mathsf{frame}` from the stack.

            2.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

            3.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

        2.  Else if the first non-value entry of the stack is not a `\mathsf{handler}`, then:

            1.  Throw the exception `{\mathit{val}'}` as a result.

        3.  Else:

            1.  Let `H` be the topmost `\mathsf{handler}`.

            2.  Let `n` be the arity of `H`

            3.  Let `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast}` be the catch handler of `H`

            4.  If `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast} = \epsilon`, then:

                1.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                2.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                3.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

            5.  Else if `a \geq {|z{.}\mathsf{exns}|}`, then:

                1.  Let `{\mathit{catch}}_0~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast}`.

                2.  If `{\mathit{catch}}_0` is some `\mathsf{catch\_all}~{\mathit{labelidx}}`, then:

                    1.  Let `(\mathsf{catch\_all}~l)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{catch}}_0`.

                    2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                    3.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

                3.  Else if `{\mathit{catch}}_0` is not some `\mathsf{catch\_all\_ref}~{\mathit{labelidx}}`, then:

                    1.  Let `{\mathit{catch}}~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast}`.

                    2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                    3.  Let `{H'}` be the `\mathsf{handler}` whose arity is `n` and whose catch handler is `{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}`.

                    4.  Push the `\mathsf{handler}` `{H'}`.

                    5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                    6.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

                4.  Else:

                    1.  Let `(\mathsf{catch\_all\_ref}~l)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{catch}}_0`.

                    2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                    3.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                    4.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

            6.  Else:

                1.  Let `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` be `z{.}\mathsf{exns}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{fields}`.

                2.  Let `{\mathit{catch}}_0~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast}`.

                3.  If `{\mathit{catch}}_0` is some `\mathsf{catch}~{\mathit{tagidx}}~{\mathit{labelidx}}`, then:

                    1.  Let `(\mathsf{catch}~x~l)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{catch}}_0`.

                    2.  If `x < {|z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}|}` and `z{.}\mathsf{exns}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{tag} = z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]`, then:

                        1.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                        2.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

                        3.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

                    3.  Else:

                        1.  Let `{\mathit{catch}}~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast}`.

                        2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                        3.  Let `{H'}` be the `\mathsf{handler}` whose arity is `n` and whose catch handler is `{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}`.

                        4.  Push the `\mathsf{handler}` `{H'}`.

                        5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                        6.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

                4.  Else if `{\mathit{catch}}_0` is some `\mathsf{catch\_ref}~{\mathit{tagidx}}~{\mathit{labelidx}}`, then:

                    1.  Let `(\mathsf{catch\_ref}~x~l)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{catch}}_0`.

                    2.  If `x \geq {|z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}|}` or `z{.}\mathsf{exns}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{tag} \neq z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]`, then:

                        1.  Let `{\mathit{catch}}~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast}`.

                        2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                        3.  Let `{H'}` be the `\mathsf{handler}` whose arity is `n` and whose catch handler is `{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}`.

                        4.  Push the `\mathsf{handler}` `{H'}`.

                        5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                        6.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

                    3.  Else:

                        1.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                        2.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

                        3.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                        4.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

                5.  Else:

                    1.  If `{\mathit{catch}}_0` is some `\mathsf{catch\_all}~{\mathit{labelidx}}`, then:

                        1.  Let `(\mathsf{catch\_all}~l)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{catch}}_0`.

                        2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                        3.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

                    2.  Else if `{\mathit{catch}}_0` is not some `\mathsf{catch\_all\_ref}~{\mathit{labelidx}}`, then:

                        1.  Let `{\mathit{catch}}~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{catch}''}^\ast}`.

                        2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                        3.  Let `H` be the `\mathsf{handler}` whose arity is `n` and whose catch handler is `{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast}`.

                        4.  Push the `\mathsf{handler}` `H`.

                        5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                        6.  Execute the instruction `\mathsf{throw\_ref}`.

                    3.  Else:

                        1.  Let `(\mathsf{catch\_all\_ref}~l)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{catch}}_0`.

                        2.  Pop the `\mathsf{handler}` from the stack.

                        3.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)` to the stack.

                        4.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{br}~l)`.

6.  Else:

    1.  Assert: Due to validation, the first non-value entry of the stack is not a `\mathsf{label}`.

    2.  Assert: Due to validation, the first non-value entry of the stack is not a `\mathsf{frame}`.

    3.  Assert: Due to validation, the first non-value entry of the stack is not a `\mathsf{handler}`.

    4.  Throw the exception `{\mathit{val}'}` as a result.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}null})~\mathsf{throw\_ref} & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} \\[0.8ex]
    & z ; {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref} &  \\
    &&& \multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{val}}^\ast} \neq \epsilon \lor {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} \neq \epsilon
    } \\[0.8ex]
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{label}}_{n}}{\{ {{\mathit{instr}'}^\ast} \}}~(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref} \\[0.8ex]
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{frame}}_{n}}{\{ f \}}~(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref} \\[0.8ex]
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{handler}}_{n}}{\{ \epsilon \}}~(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref} \\[0.8ex]
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{handler}}_{n}}{\{ (\mathsf{catch}~x~l)~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast} \}}~(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{br}~l) &  \\
    &&& \multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ z{.}\mathsf{exns}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{tag} = z{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x] \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{val}}^\ast} = z{.}\mathsf{exns}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{fields} \\
    \end{array}
    } \\[0.8ex]
    & z ; ({{\mathsf{handler}}_{n}}{\{ (\mathsf{catch\_ref}~x~l)~{{\mathit{catch}'}^\ast} \}}~(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~\mathsf{throw\_ref}) & \hookrightarrow & {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref{.}exn}~a)~(\mathsf{br}~l) &  \\
