### `\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

3.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)` from the stack.

4.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

5.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)` from the stack.

6.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

7.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)` from the stack.

8.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

9.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}}` from the stack.

10. If `{\mathit{val}} = \mathsf{ref{.}null}`, then:

    1.  Trap.

11. Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{val}}` is some `\mathsf{ref{.}array}~{\mathit{arrayaddr}}`.

12. Let `(\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{val}}`.

13. If `a < {|z{.}\mathsf{arrays}|}` and `i + n > {|z{.}\mathsf{arrays}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{fields}|}`, then:

    1.  Trap.

14. If the expansion of `z{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]` is some `\mathsf{array}~{\mathit{fieldtype}}`, then:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{array}~{\mathit{fieldtype}}_0)` be the destructuring of the expansion of `z{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x]`.

    2.  Let `({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{fieldtype}}_0`.

    3.  If `j + n \cdot {|{\mathit{zt}}|} / 8 > {|z{.}\mathsf{datas}{}[y]{.}\mathsf{bytes}|}`, then:

        1.  Trap.

    4.  If `n = 0`, then:

        1.  Do nothing.

    5.  Else:

        1.  Let `c` be the result for which `{{\mathrm{bytes}}}_{{\mathit{zt}}}(c)` `=` `z{.}\mathsf{datas}{}[y]{.}\mathsf{bytes}{}[j : {|{\mathit{zt}}|} / 8]`.

        2.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)` to the stack.

        3.  Push the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)` to the stack.

        4.  Push the value `{\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}}){.}\mathsf{const}~{{\mathrm{unpack}}}_{{\mathit{zt}}}(c)` to the stack.

        5.  Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{array{.}set}~x)`.

        6.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)` to the stack.

        7.  Push the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i + 1)` to the stack.

        8.  Push the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j + {|{\mathit{zt}}|} / 8)` to the stack.

        9.  Push the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n - 1)` to the stack.

        10. Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y)`.

15. Else if `n = 0`, then:

    1.  Do nothing.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}null})~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} \\
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} &  \\
    & \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ i + n > {|z{.}\mathsf{arrays}{}[a]{.}\mathsf{fields}|}
    } \\
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} &  \\
    & \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ z{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}}) \\
    {\land}~ j + n \cdot {|{\mathit{zt}}|} / 8 > {|z{.}\mathsf{datas}{}[y]{.}\mathsf{bytes}|} \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & \epsilon &  \\
    & \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{otherwise, if}~ n = 0
    } \\
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & & \\
    & \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}}
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}} (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~({\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathit{zt}}){.}\mathsf{const}~{{\mathrm{unpack}}}_{{\mathit{zt}}}(c))~(\mathsf{array{.}set}~x) \\
    (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i + 1)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j + {|{\mathit{zt}}|} / 8)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n - 1)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_data}~x~y) \end{array} & & \\
    \multicolumn{3}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{otherwise, if}~ z{.}\mathsf{types}{}[x] \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{array}~({\mathsf{mut}^?}~{\mathit{zt}}) \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathrm{bytes}}}_{{\mathit{zt}}}(c) = z{.}\mathsf{datas}{}[y]{.}\mathsf{bytes}{}[j : {|{\mathit{zt}}|} / 8] \\
    \end{array} \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `\mathsf{array{.}init\_elem}~x~y`

1.  Let `z` be the current state.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}` is on the top of the stack.

    10. Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{array{.}init\_elem}~x~y)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}null})~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_elem}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} \\
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_elem}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} &  \\
    & \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad

    } \\
    & z ; (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_elem}~x~y) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} &  \\

    & \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}}
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}} (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i)~{\mathit{ref}}~(\mathsf{array{.}set}~x) \\
    (\mathsf{ref{.}array}~a)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~i + 1)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~j + 1)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n - 1)~(\mathsf{array{.}init\_elem}~x~y) \end{array} & & \\
    \multicolumn{3}{@{}l@{}}{\quad

### `\mathsf{any{.}convert\_extern}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

### `\mathsf{extern{.}convert\_any}`

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathit{ref}}~\mathsf{extern{.}convert\_any} & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{ref{.}null} & \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{ref}} = \mathsf{ref{.}null} \\
    & {\mathit{ref}}~\mathsf{extern{.}convert\_any} & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{ref{.}extern}~{\mathit{ref}}) & \quad \mbox{otherwise} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

## Numeric Instructions

Numeric instructions are defined in terms of the generic numeric operators. The mapping of numeric instructions to their underlying operators is expressed by the following definition:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathit{op}_{\mathsf{i}\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}(i_1,\dots,i_k) &=& \mathrm{i}\mathit{op}_N(i_1,\dots,i_k) \\
    \mathit{op}_{\mathsf{f}\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}(z_1,\dots,z_k) &=& \mathrm{f}\mathit{op}_N(z_1,\dots,z_k) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

And for conversion operators:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathit{cvtop}^{\mathit{sx}^?}_{t_1,t_2}(c) &=& \mathit{cvtop}^{\mathit{sx}^?}_{|t_1|,|t_2|}(c) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Where the underlying operators are partial, the corresponding instruction will trap when the result is not defined. Where the underlying operators are non-deterministic, because they may return one of multiple possible NaN values, so are the corresponding instructions.

Note

For example, the result of instruction `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}.\mathsf{add}` applied to operands `i_1, i_2` invokes `\mathsf{add}_{\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}}(i_1, i_2)`, which maps to the generic `\mathrm{iadd}_{32}(i_1, i_2)` via the above definition. Similarly, `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle64}.\mathsf{trunc}\mathsf{\_}\mathsf{f\scriptstyle32}\mathsf{\_s}` applied to `z` invokes `\mathsf{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{\mathsf{f\scriptstyle32},\mathsf{i\scriptstyle64}}(z)`, which maps to the generic `\mathrm{trunc}^{\mathsf{s}}_{32,64}(z)`.

### `\mathit{nt}\mathsf{.}\mathsf{const}~c`

1.  Push the value `({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

Note

No formal reduction rule is required for this instruction, since `\mathsf{const}` instructions already are values.

### `{\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{unop}}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `{\mathit{nt}}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

3.  If `{{\mathit{unop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1)}` is empty, then:

    1.  Trap.

4.  Let `c` be an element of `{{\mathit{unop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1)}`.

5.  Push the value `({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{unop}}) & \hookrightarrow & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c \in {{\mathit{unop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1)} \\
    & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{unop}}) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} & \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{unop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1)} = \epsilon \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{binop}}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `{\mathit{nt}}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, a number value is on the top of the stack.

4.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

5.  If `{{\mathit{binop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1, c_2)}` is empty, then:

    1.  Trap.

6.  Let `c` be an element of `{{\mathit{binop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1, c_2)}`.

7.  Push the value `({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~({\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{binop}}) & \hookrightarrow & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c \in {{\mathit{binop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1, c_2)} \\
    & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~({\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{binop}}) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} & \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{binop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1, c_2)} = \epsilon \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{testop}}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `{\mathit{nt}}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

3.  Let `c` be `{{\mathit{testop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1)}`.

4.  Push the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{testop}}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = {{\mathit{testop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1)} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{relop}}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `{\mathit{nt}}` is on the top of the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, a number value is on the top of the stack.

4.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

5.  Let `c` be `{{\mathit{relop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1, c_2)}`.

6.  Push the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~({\mathit{nt}} {.} {\mathit{relop}}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = {{\mathit{relop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}}(c_1, c_2)} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{nt}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{cvtop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{nt}}_1}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of number type `{\mathit{nt}}_1` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

3.  If `{{\mathit{cvtop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}_1, {\mathit{nt}}_2}(c_1)}` is empty, then:

    1.  Trap.

4.  Let `c` be an element of `{{\mathit{cvtop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}_1, {\mathit{nt}}_2}(c_1)}`.

5.  Push the value `({\mathit{nt}}_2{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & ({\mathit{nt}}_1{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{cvtop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{nt}}_1}) & \hookrightarrow & ({\mathit{nt}}_2{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c \in {{\mathit{cvtop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}_1, {\mathit{nt}}_2}(c_1)} \\
    & ({\mathit{nt}}_1{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{nt}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{cvtop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{nt}}_1}) & \hookrightarrow & \mathsf{trap} & \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{cvtop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{nt}}_1, {\mathit{nt}}_2}(c_1)} = \epsilon \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

## Vector Instructions

Vector instructions that operate bitwise are handled as integer operations of respective bit width.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll@{\qquad}l}
    \mathit{op}_{\mathsf{v}\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}(i_1,\dots,i_k) &=& \mathrm{i}\mathit{op}_N(i_1,\dots,i_k) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Most other vector instructions are defined in terms of numeric operators that are applied lane-wise according to the given shape.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{llll}
    \mathit{op}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(n_1,\dots,n_k) &=&
    \mathrm{lanes}^{-1}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(\mathit{op}_t(i_1,\dots,i_k)^\ast) & \qquad(\mathrel{\mbox{if}} i_1^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(n_1) \land \dots \land i_k^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(n_k) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

For example, the result of instruction `\mathsf{i32x4}.\mathsf{add}` applied to operands `v_1, v_2` invokes `\mathsf{add}_{\mathsf{i32x4}}(v_1, v_2)`, which maps to `\mathrm{lanes}^{-1}_{\mathsf{i32x4}}(\mathsf{add}_{\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}}(i_1, i_2)^\ast)`, where `i_1^\ast` and `i_2^\ast` are sequences resulting from invoking `\mathrm{lanes}_{\mathsf{i32x4}}(v_1)` and `\mathrm{lanes}_{\mathsf{i32x4}}(v_2)` respectively.

For non-deterministic operators this definition is generalized to sets:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}{lll}
    \mathit{op}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(n_1,\dots,n_k) &=&
    \{ \mathrm{lanes}^{-1}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(i^\ast) ~|~ i^\ast \in {\Large\times}(\mathit{op}_t(i_1,\dots,i_k)^\ast) \land i_1^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(n_1) \land \dots \land i_k^\ast = \mathrm{lanes}_{t\mathsf{x}N}(n_k) \} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

where `{\Large\times} \{x^\ast\}^N` transforms a sequence of `N` sets of values into a set of sequences of `N` values by computing the set product:

    \begin{array}{lll}
    {\Large\times} (S_1 \dots S_N) &=& \{ x_1 \dots x_N ~|~ x_1 \in S_1 \land \dots \land x_N \in S_N \}
    \end{array}

The remaining vector operators use individual definitions.

    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{sh}}{.}\mathsf{shuffle}~{i^\ast}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

4.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

5.  Let `c` be `{\mathsf{shuffle}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}}({i^\ast}, c_1, c_2)}`.

6.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~({\mathit{sh}}{.}\mathsf{shuffle}~{i^\ast}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = {\mathsf{shuffle}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}}({i^\ast}, c_1, c_2)} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}{.}\mathsf{splat}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{numtype}}_0 = {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}})`.

4.  Let `c` be `{{{{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}^{{-1}}}}{({{{\mathrm{pack}}}_{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}(c_1)^{M}})}`.

5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & ({\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}){.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}{.}\mathsf{splat}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = {{{{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}^{{-1}}}}{({{{\mathrm{pack}}}_{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}(c_1)^{M}})} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{{{\mathit{lanetype}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}{.}\mathsf{extract\_lane}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{{\mathit{sx}'}^?}}~i`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

3.  If `{{\mathit{sx}'}^?}` is not defined, then:

    1.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{lanetype}}` is number type.

    2.  Assert: Due to validation, `i < {|{{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathit{lanetype}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1)|}`.

    3.  Let `c_2` be `{{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathit{lanetype}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1){}[i]`.

    4.  Push the value `({\mathit{lanetype}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` to the stack.

4.  Else:

    1.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{lanetype}}` is packed type.

    2.  Let `{\mathit{sx}}` be `{{\mathit{sx}'}^?}`.

    3.  Assert: Due to validation, `i < {|{{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathit{lanetype}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1)|}`.

    4.  Let `c_2` be `{{{{\mathrm{extend}}}_{{|{\mathit{lanetype}}|}, 32}^{{\mathit{sx}}}}}{({{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathit{lanetype}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1){}[i])}`.

    5.  Push the value `(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({{\mathit{nt}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}{.}\mathsf{extract\_lane}~i) & \hookrightarrow & ({\mathit{nt}}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c_2 = {{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathit{nt}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1){}[i] \\
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({{{\mathit{pt}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}{.}\mathsf{extract\_lane}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sx}}}~i) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c_2 = {{{{\mathrm{extend}}}_{{|{\mathit{pt}}|}, 32}^{{\mathit{sx}}}}}{({{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathit{pt}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1){}[i])} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}{.}\mathsf{replace\_lane}~i`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `({\mathit{numtype}}_0{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{numtype}}_0 = {\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}})`.

4.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

5.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

6.  Let `c` be `{{{{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}^{{-1}}}}{({{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1){}[{}[i] = {{\mathrm{pack}}}_{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}(c_2)])}`.

7.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathrm{unpack}}({\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}){.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~({{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}{.}\mathsf{replace\_lane}~i) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) &  \\
    & \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ c = {{{{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}^{{-1}}}}{({{\mathrm{lanes}}}_{{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}{\mathsf{x}}{M}}(c_1){}[{}[i] = {{\mathrm{pack}}}_{{\mathsf{i}}{{\scriptstyle\kern-0.1emN}}}(c_2)])}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vextunop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

3.  Let `c` be `{{\mathit{vextunop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}(c_1)}`.

4.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vextunop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{vextunop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}(c_1)} = c \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vextbinop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

4.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

5.  Let `c` be `{{\mathit{vextbinop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}(c_1, c_2)}`.

6.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~({\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vextbinop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{vextbinop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}(c_1, c_2)} = c \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vextternop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_3)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

4.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` from the stack.

5.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

6.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

7.  Let `c` be `{{\mathit{vextternop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}(c_1, c_2, c_3)}`.

8.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_3)~({\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vextternop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) &  \\
    &&& \multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{vextternop}}}{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}(c_1, c_2, c_3)} = c
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{{\mathit{sh}}_2{.}\mathsf{narrow}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sx}}}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)` from the stack.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

4.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

5.  Let `c` be `{\mathsf{narrow}}{{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}^{{\mathit{sx}}}}}{(c_1, c_2)}`.

6.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_2)~({{\mathit{sh}}_2{.}\mathsf{narrow}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sx}}}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = {\mathsf{narrow}}{{{}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}^{{\mathit{sx}}}}}{(c_1, c_2)} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vcvtop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, a value of vector type `\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}` is on the top of the stack.

2.  Pop the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)` from the stack.

3.  Let `c` be `{{\mathit{vcvtop}}}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}({\mathit{vcvtop}}, c_1)`.

4.  Push the value `(\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c)` to the stack.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c_1)~({\mathit{sh}}_2 {.} {{\mathit{vcvtop}}}{\mathsf{\_}}{{\mathit{sh}}_1}) & \hookrightarrow & (\mathsf{v\scriptstyle128}{.}\mathsf{const}~c) & \quad \mbox{if}~ c = {{\mathit{vcvtop}}}_{{\mathit{sh}}_1, {\mathit{sh}}_2}({\mathit{vcvtop}}, c_1) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

## Expressions

An expression is *evaluated* relative to a current frame pointing to its containing module instance.

### `\mathsf{eval\_expr}~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}`

1.  Execute the sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}`.

2.  Pop the value `{\mathit{val}}` from the stack.

3.  Return `{\mathit{val}}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rcl@{}l@{}}
    & z ; {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} & \hookrightarrow^\ast & {z'} ; {{\mathit{val}}^\ast} & \quad \mbox{if}~ z ; {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast} \hookrightarrow^\ast {z'} ; {{\mathit{val}}^\ast} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Evaluation iterates this reduction rule until reaching a value. Expressions constituting function bodies are executed during function invocation.

# Modules

For modules, the execution semantics primarily defines instantiation, which allocates instances for a module and its contained definitions, initializes memories and tables from contained data and element segments, and invokes the start function if present. It also includes invocation of exported functions.

## Allocation

New instances of tags, globals, memories, tables, functions, data segments, and element segments are *allocated* in a store `s`, as defined by the following auxiliary functions.

### Tags

### `{\mathrm{alloctag}}(s, {\mathit{tagtype}})`

1.  Let `{\mathit{taginst}}` be the tag instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{tagtype}} \}`.

2.  Let `a` be the length of `s{.}\mathsf{tags}`.

3.  Append `{\mathit{taginst}}` to `s{.}\mathsf{tags}`.

4.  Return `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{alloctag}}(s, {\mathit{tagtype}}) & = & (s \oplus \{ \mathsf{tags}~{\mathit{taginst}} \}, {|s{.}\mathsf{tags}|}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{taginst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{tagtype}} \}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Globals

### `{\mathrm{allocglobal}}(s, {\mathit{globaltype}}, {\mathit{val}})`

1.  Let `{\mathit{globalinst}}` be the global instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{globaltype}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{value}~{\mathit{val}} \}`.

2.  Let `a` be the length of `s{.}\mathsf{globals}`.

3.  Append `{\mathit{globalinst}}` to `s{.}\mathsf{globals}`.

4.  Return `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{allocglobal}}(s, {\mathit{globaltype}}, {\mathit{val}}) & = & (s \oplus \{ \mathsf{globals}~{\mathit{globalinst}} \}, {|s{.}\mathsf{globals}|}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{globalinst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{globaltype}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{value}~{\mathit{val}} \}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Memories

### `{\mathrm{allocmem}}(s, {\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page})`

1.  Let `{\mathit{meminst}}` be the memory instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{bytes}~{\mathtt{0x00}^{i \cdot 64 \, {\mathrm{Ki}}}} \}`.

2.  Let `a` be the length of `s{.}\mathsf{mems}`.

3.  Append `{\mathit{meminst}}` to `s{.}\mathsf{mems}`.

4.  Return `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{allocmem}}(s, {\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page}) & = & (s \oplus \{ \mathsf{mems}~{\mathit{meminst}} \}, {|s{.}\mathsf{mems}|}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{meminst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{bytes}~{(\mathtt{0x00})^{i \cdot 64 \, {\mathrm{Ki}}}} \}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Tables

### `{\mathrm{alloctable}}(s, {\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}, {\mathit{ref}})`

1.  Let `{\mathit{tableinst}}` be the table instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{refs}~{{\mathit{ref}}^{i}} \}`.

2.  Let `a` be the length of `s{.}\mathsf{tables}`.

3.  Append `{\mathit{tableinst}}` to `s{.}\mathsf{tables}`.

4.  Return `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{alloctable}}(s, {\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}, {\mathit{ref}}) & = & (s \oplus \{ \mathsf{tables}~{\mathit{tableinst}} \}, {|s{.}\mathsf{tables}|}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{tableinst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{refs}~{{\mathit{ref}}^{i}} \}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Functions

### `{\mathrm{allocfunc}}(s, {\mathit{deftype}}, {{\mathit{code}}}, {\mathit{moduleinst}})`

1.  Let `{\mathit{funcinst}}` be the function instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{deftype}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{module}~{\mathit{moduleinst}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{code}~{{\mathit{code}}} \}`.

2.  Let `a` be the length of `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}`.

3.  Append `{\mathit{funcinst}}` to `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}`.

4.  Return `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{allocfunc}}(s, {\mathit{deftype}}, {{\mathit{code}}}, {\mathit{moduleinst}}) & = & (s \oplus \{ \mathsf{funcs}~{\mathit{funcinst}} \}, {|s{.}\mathsf{funcs}|}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{funcinst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{deftype}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{module}~{\mathit{moduleinst}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{code}~{{\mathit{code}}} \}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Data segments

### `{\mathrm{allocdata}}(s, \mathsf{ok}, {{\mathit{byte}}^\ast})`

1.  Let `{\mathit{datainst}}` be the data instance `\{ \mathsf{bytes}~{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast} \}`.

2.  Let `a` be the length of `s{.}\mathsf{datas}`.

3.  Append `{\mathit{datainst}}` to `s{.}\mathsf{datas}`.

4.  Return `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{allocdata}}(s, \mathsf{ok}, {{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}) & = & (s \oplus \{ \mathsf{datas}~{\mathit{datainst}} \}, {|s{.}\mathsf{datas}|}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{datainst}} = \{ \mathsf{bytes}~{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast} \}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Element segments

### `{\mathrm{allocelem}}(s, {\mathit{elemtype}}, {{\mathit{ref}}^\ast})`

1.  Let `{\mathit{eleminst}}` be the element instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{elemtype}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{refs}~{{\mathit{ref}}^\ast} \}`.

2.  Let `a` be the length of `s{.}\mathsf{elems}`.

3.  Append `{\mathit{eleminst}}` to `s{.}\mathsf{elems}`.

4.  Return `a`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{allocelem}}(s, {\mathit{elemtype}}, {{\mathit{ref}}^\ast}) & = & (s \oplus \{ \mathsf{elems}~{\mathit{eleminst}} \}, {|s{.}\mathsf{elems}|}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{eleminst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{elemtype}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{refs}~{{\mathit{ref}}^\ast} \}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Growing memories

### `{\mathrm{growmem}}({\mathit{meminst}}, n)`

1.  Let `\{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{bytes}~{b^\ast} \}` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{meminst}}`.

2.  Let `{i'}` be `{|{b^\ast}|} / (64 \, {\mathrm{Ki}}) + n`.

3.  If not `{({i'} \leq j)^?}`, then:

    1.  Fail.

4.  If `{i'} \leq {2^{{|{\mathit{at}}|} - 16}}`, then:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{meminst}'}` be the memory instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ {i'} \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{bytes}~{b^\ast}~{\mathtt{0x00}^{n \cdot 64 \, {\mathrm{Ki}}}} \}`.

    2.  Return `{\mathit{meminst}'}`.

5.  Fail.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{growmem}}({\mathit{meminst}}, n) & = & {\mathit{meminst}'} & \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{meminst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page}),\; \mathsf{bytes}~{b^\ast} \} \\
    {\land}~ {\mathit{meminst}'} = \{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ {i'} \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~\mathsf{page}),\; \mathsf{bytes}~{b^\ast}~{(\mathtt{0x00})^{n \cdot 64 \, {\mathrm{Ki}}}} \} \\
    {\land}~ {i'} = {|{b^\ast}|} / (64 \, {\mathrm{Ki}}) + n \\
    {\land}~ ({i'} \leq j)^? \\
    {\land}~ {i'} \leq {2^{{|{\mathit{at}}|} - 16}} \\
    \end{array} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Growing tables

### `{\mathrm{growtable}}({\mathit{tableinst}}, n, r)`

1.  Let `\{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{refs}~{{r'}^\ast} \}` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{tableinst}}`.

2.  Let `{i'}` be `{|{{r'}^\ast}|} + n`.

3.  If not `{({i'} \leq j)^?}`, then:

    1.  Fail.

4.  If `{i'} \leq {2^{{|{\mathit{at}}|}}} - 1`, then:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{tableinst}'}` be the table instance `\{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ {i'} \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{refs}~{{r'}^\ast}~{r^{n}} \}`.

    2.  Return `{\mathit{tableinst}'}`.

5.  Fail.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{growtable}}({\mathit{tableinst}}, n, r) & = & {\mathit{tableinst}'} & \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{tableinst}} = \{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ i \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}),\; \mathsf{refs}~{{r'}^\ast} \} \\
    {\land}~ {\mathit{tableinst}'} = \{ \mathsf{type}~({\mathit{at}}~{}[ {i'} \,{..}\, {j^?} ]~{\mathit{rt}}),\; \mathsf{refs}~{{r'}^\ast}~{r^{n}} \} \\
    {\land}~ {i'} = {|{{r'}^\ast}|} + n \\
    {\land}~ ({i'} \leq j)^? \\
    {\land}~ {i'} \leq {2^{{|{\mathit{at}}|}}} - 1 \\
    \end{array} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### Modules

### `{\mathrm{allocmodule}}(s, {\mathit{module}}, {{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}, {{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast})`

1.  Let `(\mathsf{module}~{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{import}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{tag}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{start}}^?}~{{\mathit{export}}^\ast})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{module}}`.

2.  Let `{{\mathit{aa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` be `{\mathrm{tags}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})`.

3.  Let `{{\mathit{ga}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` be `{\mathrm{globals}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})`.

4.  Let `{{\mathit{fa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` be `{\mathrm{funcs}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})`.

5.  Let `{{\mathit{ma}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` be `{\mathrm{mems}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})`.

6.  Let `{{\mathit{ta}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}` be `{\mathrm{tables}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})`.

7.  Let `{{\mathit{fa}}^\ast}` be `{|s{.}\mathsf{funcs}|} + i_{\mathsf{f}}` for all `i_{\mathsf{f}}` from `0` to `{|{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}|} - 1`.

8.  Let `{{\mathit{tagtype}}^\ast}` be the tag type sequence `\epsilon`.

9.  For each `{\mathit{tag}}` in `{{\mathit{tag}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{tagtype}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{tag}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{tagtype}}` to `{{\mathit{tagtype}}^\ast}`.

10. Let `{{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}^\ast}` be the byte sequence sequence `\epsilon`.

11. For each `{\mathit{data}}` in `{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{data}~{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}~{\mathit{datamode}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{data}}`.

    2.  Append `{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}` to `{{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}^\ast}`.

12. Let `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}` be the global type sequence `\epsilon`.

13. For each `{\mathit{global}}` in `{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globaltype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{global}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{globaltype}}` to `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}`.

14. Let `{{\mathit{tabletype}}^\ast}` be the table type sequence `\epsilon`.

15. For each `{\mathit{table}}` in `{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tabletype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{table}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{tabletype}}` to `{{\mathit{tabletype}}^\ast}`.

16. Let `{{\mathit{memtype}}^\ast}` be the memory type sequence `\epsilon`.

17. For each `{\mathit{mem}}` in `{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{memory}~{\mathit{memtype}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{mem}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{memtype}}` to `{{\mathit{memtype}}^\ast}`.

18. Let `{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}` be `{{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}}^\ast})}`.

19. Let `{{\mathit{elemtype}}^\ast}` be the reference type sequence `\epsilon`.

20. For each `{\mathit{elem}}` in `{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{elemtype}}~{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}~{\mathit{elemmode}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{elem}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{elemtype}}` to `{{\mathit{elemtype}}^\ast}`.

21. Let `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}}^\ast}` be the expression sequence `\epsilon`.

22. Let `{{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}^\ast}` be the local sequence sequence `\epsilon`.

23. Let `{x^\ast}` be the type index sequence `\epsilon`.

24. For each `{\mathit{func}}` in `{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{func}~x~{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{func}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}}` to `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}}^\ast}`.

    3.  Append `{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}` to `{{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}^\ast}`.

    4.  Append `x` to `{x^\ast}`.

25. Let `{{\mathit{aa}}^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

26. For each `{\mathit{tagtype}}` in `{{\mathit{tagtype}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{aa}}` be the tag address `{\mathrm{alloctag}}(s, {{\mathit{tagtype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{aa}}` to `{{\mathit{aa}}^\ast}`.

27. Let `{{\mathit{ga}}^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

28. For each `{\mathit{globaltype}}` in `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}` and `{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}` in `{{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{ga}}` be the global address `{\mathrm{allocglobal}}(s, {{\mathit{globaltype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}, {\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{ga}}` to `{{\mathit{ga}}^\ast}`.

29. Let `{{\mathit{ma}}^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

30. For each `{\mathit{memtype}}` in `{{\mathit{memtype}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{ma}}` be the memory address `{\mathrm{allocmem}}(s, {{\mathit{memtype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{ma}}` to `{{\mathit{ma}}^\ast}`.

31. Let `{{\mathit{ta}}^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

32. For each `{\mathit{tabletype}}` in `{{\mathit{tabletype}}^\ast}` and `{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}` in `{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{ta}}` be the table address `{\mathrm{alloctable}}(s, {{\mathit{tabletype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}, {\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{ta}}` to `{{\mathit{ta}}^\ast}`.

33. Let `{{\mathit{xi}}^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

34. For each `{\mathit{export}}` in `{{\mathit{export}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{xi}}` be the export instance `{\mathrm{allocexport}}({\mathit{moduleinst}}, {\mathit{export}})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{xi}}` to `{{\mathit{xi}}^\ast}`.

35. Let `{{\mathit{da}}^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

36. For each `{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}` in `{{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{da}}` be the data address `{\mathrm{allocdata}}(s, \mathsf{ok}, {{\mathit{byte}}^\ast})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{da}}` to `{{\mathit{da}}^\ast}`.

37. Let `{{\mathit{ea}}^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

38. For each `{\mathit{elemtype}}` in `{{\mathit{elemtype}}^\ast}` and `{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}` in `{{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{ea}}` be the elem address `{\mathrm{allocelem}}(s, {{\mathit{elemtype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}, {{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{ea}}` to `{{\mathit{ea}}^\ast}`.

39. Let `{\mathit{moduleinst}}` be the module instance `\{ \mathsf{types}~{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{tags}~{{\mathit{aa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{aa}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{globals}~{{\mathit{ga}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ga}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{mems}~{{\mathit{ma}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ma}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{tables}~{{\mathit{ta}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ta}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{funcs}~{{\mathit{fa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{fa}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{datas}~{{\mathit{da}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{elems}~{{\mathit{ea}}^\ast},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{exports}~{{\mathit{xi}}^\ast} \}`.

40. Let `{{\mathit{funcaddr}}_0^\ast}` be `\epsilon`.

41. For each `{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}}` in `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}}^\ast}` and `{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}` in `{{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}^\ast}` and `x` in `{x^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{funcaddr}}_0` be the function address `{\mathrm{allocfunc}}(s, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}{}[x], \mathsf{func}~x~{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}}, {\mathit{moduleinst}})`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{funcaddr}}_0` to `{{\mathit{funcaddr}}_0^\ast}`.

42. Assert: Due to validation, `{{\mathit{funcaddr}}_0^\ast} = {{\mathit{fa}}^\ast}`.

43. Return `{\mathit{moduleinst}}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{allocmodule}}(s, {\mathit{module}}, {{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}, {({{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast})^\ast}) & = & (s_7, {\mathit{moduleinst}}) &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ {\mathit{module}} = \mathsf{module}~{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{import}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{tag}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{start}}^?}~{{\mathit{export}}^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{tag}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{tagtype}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{global}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globaltype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{mem}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{memory}~{\mathit{memtype}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{table}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tabletype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{func}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{func}~x~{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{data}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{data}~{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}~{\mathit{datamode}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{elem}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{elemtype}}~{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}~{\mathit{elemmode}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{aa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast} = {\mathrm{tags}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}) \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{ga}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast} = {\mathrm{globals}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}) \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{ma}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast} = {\mathrm{mems}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}) \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{ta}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast} = {\mathrm{tables}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}) \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{fa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast} = {\mathrm{funcs}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}) \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} = {{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{fa}}^\ast} = {({|s{.}\mathsf{funcs}|} + i_{\mathsf{f}})^{i_{\mathsf{f}}<{|{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}|}}} \\
    {\land}~ (s_1, {{\mathit{aa}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{alloctag}}^\ast}}{(s, {{{\mathit{tagtype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ (s_2, {{\mathit{ga}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{allocglobal}}^\ast}}{(s_1, {{{\mathit{globaltype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}^\ast}, {{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ (s_3, {{\mathit{ma}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{allocmem}}^\ast}}{(s_2, {{{\mathit{memtype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ (s_4, {{\mathit{ta}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{alloctable}}^\ast}}{(s_3, {{{\mathit{tabletype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}^\ast}, {{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ (s_5, {{\mathit{da}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{allocdata}}^\ast}}{(s_4, {\mathsf{ok}^{{|{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}|}}}, {({{\mathit{byte}}^\ast})^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ (s_6, {{\mathit{ea}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{allocelem}}^\ast}}{(s_5, {{{\mathit{elemtype}}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{dt}}^\ast} ]}^\ast}, {({{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast})^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ (s_7, {{\mathit{fa}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{allocfunc}}^\ast}}{(s_6, {{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast}{}[x]^\ast}, {(\mathsf{func}~x~{{\mathit{local}}^\ast}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{f}})^\ast}, {{\mathit{moduleinst}}^{{|{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}|}}})} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{xi}}^\ast} = {{{\mathrm{allocexport}}^\ast}}{(\{ \mathsf{tags}~{{\mathit{aa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{aa}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{globals}~{{\mathit{ga}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ga}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{mems}~{{\mathit{ma}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ma}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{tables}~{{\mathit{ta}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ta}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{funcs}~{{\mathit{fa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{fa}}^\ast} \}, {{\mathit{export}}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ {\mathit{moduleinst}} = \{ \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mathsf{types}~{{\mathit{dt}}^\ast},\; \\
    \mathsf{tags}~{{\mathit{aa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{aa}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{globals}~{{\mathit{ga}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ga}}^\ast},\; \\
    \mathsf{mems}~{{\mathit{ma}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ma}}^\ast},\; \\
    \mathsf{tables}~{{\mathit{ta}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{ta}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{funcs}~{{\mathit{fa}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{fa}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{datas}~{{\mathit{da}}^\ast},\; \\
    \mathsf{elems}~{{\mathit{ea}}^\ast},\; \mathsf{exports}~{{\mathit{xi}}^\ast} \}\end{array} \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Here, the notation `\mathrm{allocx}^\ast` is shorthand for multiple allocations of object kind `X`, defined as follows:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {{{\mathrm{allocX}}^\ast}}{(s, \epsilon, \epsilon)} & = & (s, \epsilon) \\
    {{{\mathrm{allocX}}^\ast}}{(s, X~{{X'}^\ast}, Y~{{Y'}^\ast})} & = & (s_2, a~{{a'}^\ast}) & \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ (s_1, a) = {\mathrm{allocX}}(X, Y, s, X, Y) \\
    {\land}~ (s_2, {{a'}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{allocX}}^\ast}}{(s_1, {{X'}^\ast}, {{Y'}^\ast})} \\
    \end{array} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

For types, however, allocation is defined in terms of rolling and substitution of all preceding types to produce a list of closed defined types:

### `{{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}''}^\ast})}`

1.  If `{{\mathit{type}''}^\ast} = \epsilon`, then:

    1.  Return `\epsilon`.

2.  Let `{{\mathit{type}'}^\ast}~{\mathit{type}}` be `{{\mathit{type}''}^\ast}`.

3.  Let `(\mathsf{type}~{\mathit{rectype}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{type}}`.

4.  Let `{{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast}` be `{{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}'}^\ast})}`.

5.  Let `x` be the length of `{{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast}`.

6.  Let `{{\mathit{deftype}}^\ast}` be `{{{{{\mathrm{roll}}}_{x}^\ast}}{({\mathit{rectype}})}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast} ]}`.

7.  Return `{{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast}~{{\mathit{deftype}}^\ast}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{(\epsilon)} & = & \epsilon \\
    {{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}'}^\ast}~{\mathit{type}})} & = & {{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast}~{{\mathit{deftype}}^\ast} & \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ {{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast} = {{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}'}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ {\mathit{type}} = \mathsf{type}~{\mathit{rectype}} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{deftype}}^\ast} = {{{{{\mathrm{roll}}}_{x}^\ast}}{({\mathit{rectype}})}}{{}[ {\mathrel{:=}}\, {{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast} ]} \\
    {\land}~ x = {|{{\mathit{deftype}'}^\ast}|} \\
    \end{array} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Finally, export instances are produced with the help of the following definition:

### `{\mathrm{allocexport}}({\mathit{moduleinst}}, \mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~{\mathit{externidx}})`

1.  If `{\mathit{externidx}}` is some `\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{tagidx}}`, then:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{tag}~x)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{externidx}}`.

    2.  Return `\{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]) \}`.

2.  If `{\mathit{externidx}}` is some `\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globalidx}}`, then:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{global}~x)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{externidx}}`.

    2.  Return `\{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]) \}`.

3.  If `{\mathit{externidx}}` is some `\mathsf{memory}~{\mathit{memidx}}`, then:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{memory}~x)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{externidx}}`.

    2.  Return `\{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{mem}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]) \}`.

4.  If `{\mathit{externidx}}` is some `\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tableidx}}`, then:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{table}~x)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{externidx}}`.

    2.  Return `\{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]) \}`.

5.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{externidx}}` is some `\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{funcidx}}`.

6.  Let `(\mathsf{func}~x)` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{externidx}}`.

7.  Return `\{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]) \}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{allocexport}}({\mathit{moduleinst}}, \mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~(\mathsf{tag}~x)) & = & \{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{tag}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{tags}{}[x]) \} \\
    {\mathrm{allocexport}}({\mathit{moduleinst}}, \mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~(\mathsf{global}~x)) & = & \{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{globals}{}[x]) \} \\
    {\mathrm{allocexport}}({\mathit{moduleinst}}, \mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~(\mathsf{memory}~x)) & = & \{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{mem}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{mems}{}[x]) \} \\
    {\mathrm{allocexport}}({\mathit{moduleinst}}, \mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~(\mathsf{table}~x)) & = & \{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{tables}{}[x]) \} \\
    {\mathrm{allocexport}}({\mathit{moduleinst}}, \mathsf{export}~{\mathit{name}}~(\mathsf{func}~x)) & = & \{ \mathsf{name}~{\mathit{name}},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{addr}~(\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[x]) \} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

The definition of module allocation is mutually recursive with the allocation of its associated functions, because the resulting module instance is passed to the allocators as an argument, in order to form the necessary closures. In an implementation, this recursion is easily unraveled by mutating one or the other in a secondary step.

## Instantiation

Given a store `s`, a `{\mathit{module}}` is instantiated with a list of external addresses `{{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}` supplying the required imports as follows.

Instantiation checks that the module is valid and the provided imports match the declared types, and may *fail* with an error otherwise. Instantiation can also result in an exception or trap when initializing a table or memory from an active segment or when executing the start function. It is up to the embedder to define how such conditions are reported.

### `{\mathrm{instantiate}}(s, {\mathit{module}}, {{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})`

1.  If `{\mathit{module}}` is not valid, then:

    1.  Fail.

2.  Let `{{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}~\mathrel{\rightarrow}~{{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}` be the destructuring of the type of `{\mathit{module}}`.

3.  Let `(\mathsf{module}~{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{import}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{tag}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{start}}^?}~{{\mathit{export}}^\ast})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{module}}`.

4.  If `{|{{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}|} \neq {|{{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}|}`, then:

    1.  Fail.

5.  For all `{\mathit{externaddr}}` in `{{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}`, and corresponding `{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}` in `{{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast}`:

    1.  If `{\mathit{externaddr}}` is not valid with type `{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}`, then:

        1.  Fail.

6.  Let `{{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{d}}^\ast}` be the concatenation of `{{{\mathrm{rundata}}}_{i_{\mathsf{d}}}({{\mathit{data}}^\ast}{}[i_{\mathsf{d}}])^{i_{\mathsf{d}}<{|{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}|}}}`.

7.  Let `{{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}` be the concatenation of `{{{\mathrm{runelem}}}_{i_{\mathsf{e}}}({{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}{}[i_{\mathsf{e}}])^{i_{\mathsf{e}}<{|{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}|}}}`.

8.  Let `{\mathit{moduleinst}}_0` be the module instance `\{ \mathsf{types}~{{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}}^\ast})},\;\allowbreak \mathsf{globals}~{\mathrm{globals}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}),\;\allowbreak \mathsf{funcs}~{\mathrm{funcs}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})~{({|s{.}\mathsf{funcs}|} + i_{\mathsf{f}})^{i_{\mathsf{f}}<{|{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}|}}} \}`.

9.  Let `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}` be the expression sequence `\epsilon`.

10. For each `{\mathit{table}}` in `{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tabletype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{table}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}}` to `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}`.

11. Let `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}` be the expression sequence `\epsilon`.

12. Let `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}` be the global type sequence `\epsilon`.

13. For each `{\mathit{global}}` in `{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globaltype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{global}}`.

    2.  Append `{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}}` to `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}`.

    3.  Append `{\mathit{globaltype}}` to `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}`.

14. Let `{{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast}` be the expression sequence sequence `\epsilon`.

15. For each `{\mathit{elem}}` in `{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}`, do:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{reftype}}~{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}~{\mathit{elemmode}})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{elem}}`.

    2.  Append `{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}` to `{{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast}`.

16. Let `z` be the state `(s, \{ \mathsf{module}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}_0 \})`.

17. Let `F` be the `\mathsf{frame}` `z{.}\mathsf{frame}`.

18. Push the `\mathsf{frame}` `F`.

19. Let `{{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}` be `{{{\mathrm{evalglobal}}^\ast}}{(z, {{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast})}`.

20. Let `{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}` be `{{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}}{(z, {{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast})}`.

21. Let `{{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast}` be `{{{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}^\ast}}{(z, {{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast})}`.

22. Pop the `\mathsf{frame}` from the stack.

23. Let `(s, f)` be the destructuring of `z`.

24. Let `{\mathit{moduleinst}}` be `{\mathrm{allocmodule}}(s, {\mathit{module}}, {{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}, {{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast})`.

25. Let `{F'}` be the `\mathsf{frame}` `\{ \mathsf{module}~{\mathit{moduleinst}} \}`.

26. Push the `\mathsf{frame}` `{F'}`.

27. Execute the sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}`.

28. Execute the sequence `{{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{d}}^\ast}`.

29. If `{{\mathit{start}}^?}` is defined, then:

    1.  Let `(\mathsf{start}~x)` be `{{\mathit{start}}^?}`.

    2.  Let `{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{s}}` be the instruction `(\mathsf{call}~x)`.

    3.  Execute the instruction `{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{s}}`.

30. Pop the `\mathsf{frame}` from the stack.

31. Return `{\mathit{moduleinst}}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{instantiate}}(s, {\mathit{module}}, {{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}) & = & {s''''} ; \{ \mathsf{module}~{\mathit{moduleinst}} \} ; {{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{d}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{s}}^?} &  \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ {\vdash}\, {\mathit{module}} : {{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}}^\ast} \mathrel{\rightarrow} {{\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ (s \vdash {\mathit{externaddr}} : {\mathit{xt}}_{\mathsf{i}})^\ast \\[0.8ex]
    {\land}~ {\mathit{module}} = \mathsf{module}~{{\mathit{type}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{import}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{tag}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{global}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{mem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{table}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}~{{\mathit{start}}^?}~{{\mathit{export}}^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{global}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{global}~{\mathit{globaltype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{table}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{table}~{\mathit{tabletype}}~{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{data}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{data}~{{\mathit{byte}}^\ast}~{\mathit{datamode}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{elem}}^\ast} = {(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{reftype}}~{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}~{\mathit{elemmode}})^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{start}}^?} = {(\mathsf{start}~x)^?} \\
    {\land}~ {\mathit{moduleinst}}_0 = \{ \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mathsf{types}~{{{\mathrm{alloctype}}^\ast}}{({{\mathit{type}}^\ast})},\; \\
    \mathsf{globals}~{\mathrm{globals}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}),\; \\
    \mathsf{funcs}~{\mathrm{funcs}}({{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast})~{({|s{.}\mathsf{funcs}|} + i_{\mathsf{f}})^{i_{\mathsf{f}}<{|{{\mathit{func}}^\ast}|}}} \}\end{array} \\
    {\land}~ z = s ; \{ \mathsf{module}~{\mathit{moduleinst}}_0 \} \\
    {\land}~ ({z'}, {{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{evalglobal}}^\ast}}{(z, {{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ ({z''}, {{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}}{({z'}, {{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ ({z'''}, {{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast}) = {{{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}^\ast}}{({z''}, {{{\mathit{expr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast})} \\
    {\land}~ {z'''} = {s'''} ; f \\
    {\land}~ ({s''''}, {\mathit{moduleinst}}) = {\mathrm{allocmodule}}({s'''}, {\mathit{module}}, {{\mathit{externaddr}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}^\ast}, {({{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast})^\ast}) \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{d}}^\ast} = {\bigoplus}\, {{{\mathrm{rundata}}}_{i_{\mathsf{d}}}({{\mathit{data}}^\ast}{}[i_{\mathsf{d}}])^{i_{\mathsf{d}}<{|{{\mathit{data}}^\ast}|}}} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast} = {\bigoplus}\, {{{\mathrm{runelem}}}_{i_{\mathsf{e}}}({{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}{}[i_{\mathsf{e}}])^{i_{\mathsf{e}}<{|{{\mathit{elem}}^\ast}|}}} \\
    {\land}~ {{\mathit{instr}}_{\mathsf{s}}^?} = {(\mathsf{call}~x)^?} \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

where:

### `{{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}}{(z, {{\mathit{expr}''}^\ast})}`

1.  If `{{\mathit{expr}''}^\ast} = \epsilon`, then:

    1.  Return `\epsilon`.

2.  Let `{\mathit{expr}}~{{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{expr}''}^\ast}`.

3.  Let `{\mathit{ref}}` be the result of evaluating `{\mathit{expr}}` with state `z`.

4.  Let `{{\mathit{ref}'}^\ast}` be `{{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}}{(z, {{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast})}`.

5.  Return `{\mathit{ref}}~{{\mathit{ref}'}^\ast}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}}{(z, \epsilon)} & = & (z, \epsilon) \\
    {{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}}{(z, {\mathit{expr}}~{{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast})} & = & ({z''}, {\mathit{ref}}~{{\mathit{ref}'}^\ast}) &  \\
    && \multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ z ; {\mathit{expr}} \hookrightarrow^\ast {z'} ; {\mathit{ref}} \\
    {\land}~ ({z''}, {{\mathit{ref}'}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{evalexpr}}^\ast}}{({z'}, {{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast})} \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

and:

### `{{{\mathrm{evalglobal}}^\ast}}{(z, {{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}, {{\mathit{expr}''}^\ast})}`

1.  If `{{\mathit{expr}''}^\ast} = \epsilon`, then:

    1.  Assert: Due to validation, `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast} = \epsilon`.

    2.  Return `\epsilon`.

2.  Else:

    1.  Let `{\mathit{expr}}~{{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{expr}''}^\ast}`.

    2.  Assert: Due to validation, `{|{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}|} \geq 1`.

    3.  Let `{\mathit{gt}}~{{\mathit{gt}'}^\ast}` be `{{\mathit{globaltype}}^\ast}`.

    4.  Let `{\mathit{val}}` be the result of evaluating `{\mathit{expr}}` with state `z`.

    5.  Let `(s, f)` be the destructuring of `z`.

    6.  Let `a` be `{\mathrm{allocglobal}}(s, {\mathit{gt}}, {\mathit{val}})`.

    7.  Append `a` to `f{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{globals}`.

    8.  Let `{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}` be `{{{\mathrm{evalglobal}}^\ast}}{((s, f), {{\mathit{gt}'}^\ast}, {{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast})}`.

    9.  Return `{\mathit{val}}~{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {{{\mathrm{evalglobal}}^\ast}}{(z, \epsilon, \epsilon)} & = & (z, \epsilon) \\
    {{{\mathrm{evalglobal}}^\ast}}{(z, {\mathit{gt}}~{{\mathit{gt}'}^\ast}, {\mathit{expr}}~{{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast})} & = & ({z''}, {\mathit{val}}~{{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}) &  \\
    && \multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ z ; {\mathit{expr}} \hookrightarrow^\ast {z'} ; {\mathit{val}} \\
    {\land}~ {z'} = s ; f \\
    {\land}~ ({s'}, a) = {\mathrm{allocglobal}}(s, {\mathit{gt}}, {\mathit{val}}) \\
    {\land}~ ({z''}, {{\mathit{val}'}^\ast}) = {{{\mathrm{evalglobal}}^\ast}}{(({s'} ; f{}[{.}\mathsf{module}{.}\mathsf{globals} \mathrel{{=}{\oplus}} a]), {{\mathit{gt}'}^\ast}, {{\mathit{expr}'}^\ast})} \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

### `{{\mathrm{rundata}}}_{x}(\mathsf{data}~{b^{n}}~{\mathit{datamode}})`

1.  If `{\mathit{datamode}} = \mathsf{passive}`, then:

    1.  Return `\epsilon`.

2.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{datamode}}` is some `\mathsf{active}~{\mathit{memidx}}~{\mathit{expr}}`.

3.  Let `(\mathsf{active}~y~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{datamode}}`.

4.  Return `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~0)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{memory{.}init}~y~x)~(\mathsf{data{.}drop}~x)`.

### `{{\mathrm{runelem}}}_{x}(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{rt}}~{e^{n}}~{\mathit{elemmode}})`

1.  If `{\mathit{elemmode}} = \mathsf{passive}`, then:

    1.  Return `\epsilon`.

2.  If `{\mathit{elemmode}} = \mathsf{declare}`, then:

    1.  Return `(\mathsf{elem{.}drop}~x)`.

3.  Assert: Due to validation, `{\mathit{elemmode}}` is some `\mathsf{active}~{\mathit{tableidx}}~{\mathit{expr}}`.

4.  Let `(\mathsf{active}~y~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast})` be the destructuring of `{\mathit{elemmode}}`.

5.  Return `{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~0)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{table{.}init}~y~x)~(\mathsf{elem{.}drop}~x)`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {{\mathrm{rundata}}}_{x}(\mathsf{data}~{b^{n}}~(\mathsf{passive})) & = & \epsilon \\
    {{\mathrm{rundata}}}_{x}(\mathsf{data}~{b^{n}}~(\mathsf{active}~y~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast})) & = & & \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~0)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{memory{.}init}~y~x)~(\mathsf{data{.}drop}~x) \\
    \end{array}
    } \\[0.8ex]
    {{\mathrm{runelem}}}_{x}(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{rt}}~{e^{n}}~(\mathsf{passive})) & = & \epsilon \\
    {{\mathrm{runelem}}}_{x}(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{rt}}~{e^{n}}~(\mathsf{declare})) & = & (\mathsf{elem{.}drop}~x) \\
    {{\mathrm{runelem}}}_{x}(\mathsf{elem}~{\mathit{rt}}~{e^{n}}~(\mathsf{active}~y~{{\mathit{instr}}^\ast})) & = & & \\
    \multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    {{\mathit{instr}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~0)~(\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}{.}\mathsf{const}~n)~(\mathsf{table{.}init}~y~x)~(\mathsf{elem{.}drop}~x) \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Note

Checking import types assumes that the module instance has already been allocated to compute the respective closed defined types. However, this forward reference merely is a way to simplify the specification. In practice, implementations will likely allocate or canonicalize types beforehand, when *compiling* a module, in a stage before instantiation and before imports are checked.

Similarly, module allocation and the evaluation of global and table initializers as well as element segments are mutually recursive because the global initialization values `{{\mathit{val}}_{\mathsf{g}}^\ast}`, `{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{t}}`, and element segment contents `{{{\mathit{ref}}_{\mathsf{e}}^\ast}^\ast}` are passed to the module allocator while depending on the module instance `{\mathit{moduleinst}}` and store `{s'}` returned by allocation. Again, this recursion is just a specification device. In practice, the initialization values can be determined beforehand by staging module allocation such that first, the module’s own function instances are pre-allocated in the store, then the initializer expressions are evaluated in order, allocating globals on the way, then the rest of the module instance is allocated, and finally the new function instances’ `\mathsf{module}` fields are set to that module instance. This is possible because validation ensures that initialization expressions cannot actually call a function, only take their reference.

All failure conditions are checked before any observable mutation of the store takes place. Store mutation is not atomic; it happens in individual steps that may be interleaved with other threads.

Evaluation of constant expressions does not affect the store.

## Invocation

Once a module has been instantiated, any exported function can be *invoked* externally via its function address `{\mathit{funcaddr}}` in the store `s` and an appropriate list `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` of argument values.

Invocation may *fail* with an error if the arguments do not fit the function type. Invocation can also result in an exception or trap. It is up to the embedder to define how such conditions are reported.

Note

If the embedder API performs type checks itself, either statically or dynamically, before performing an invocation, then no failure other than traps or exceptions can occur.

### `{\mathrm{invoke}}(s, {\mathit{funcaddr}}, {{\mathit{val}}^\ast})`

1.  Assert: Due to validation, the expansion of `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[{\mathit{funcaddr}}]{.}\mathsf{type}` is some `\mathsf{func}~{\mathit{resulttype}} \rightarrow {\mathit{resulttype}}`.

2.  Let `(\mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast}~\rightarrow~{t_2^\ast})` be the destructuring of the expansion of `s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[{\mathit{funcaddr}}]{.}\mathsf{type}`.

3.  If `{|{t_1^\ast}|} \neq {|{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}|}`, then:

    1.  Fail.

4.  For all `t_1` in `{t_1^\ast}`, and corresponding `{\mathit{val}}` in `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}`:

    1.  If `{\mathit{val}}` is not valid with type `t_1`, then:

        1.  Fail.

5.  Let `k` be the length of `{t_2^\ast}`.

6.  Let `F` be the `\mathsf{frame}` `\{ \mathsf{module}~\{ \} \}` whose arity is `k`.

7.  Push the `\mathsf{frame}` `F`.

8.  Push the values `{{\mathit{val}}^\ast}` to the stack.

9.  Push the value `(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~{\mathit{funcaddr}})` to the stack.

10. Execute the instruction `(\mathsf{call\_ref}~s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[{\mathit{funcaddr}}]{.}\mathsf{type})`.

11. Pop the values `{{\mathit{val}'}^{k}}` from the stack.

12. Pop the `\mathsf{frame}` from the stack.

13. Return `{{\mathit{val}'}^{k}}`.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}lcl@{}l@{}}
    {\mathrm{invoke}}(s, {\mathit{funcaddr}}, {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}) & = & s ; \{ \mathsf{module}~\{  \} \} ; {{\mathit{val}}^\ast}~(\mathsf{ref{.}func}~{\mathit{funcaddr}})~(\mathsf{call\_ref}~s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[{\mathit{funcaddr}}]{.}\mathsf{type}) &  \\
    && \multicolumn{2}{@{}l@{}}{\quad
    \quad
    \begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}}
    \mbox{if}~ s{.}\mathsf{funcs}{}[{\mathit{funcaddr}}]{.}\mathsf{type} \mathrel{\approx} \mathsf{func}~{t_1^\ast} \rightarrow {t_2^\ast} \\
    {\land}~ (s \vdash {\mathit{val}} : t_1)^\ast \\
    \end{array}
    } \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

# Conventions

The binary format for WebAssembly modules is a dense linear *encoding* of their abstract syntax. \[1\]

The format is defined by an *attribute grammar* whose only terminal symbols are bytes. A byte sequence is a well-formed encoding of a module if and only if it is generated by the grammar.

Each production of this grammar has exactly one synthesized attribute: the abstract syntax that the respective byte sequence encodes. Thus, the attribute grammar implicitly defines a *decoding* function (i.e., a parsing function for the binary format).

Except for a few exceptions, the binary grammar closely mirrors the grammar of the abstract syntax.

Note

Some phrases of abstract syntax have multiple possible encodings in the binary format. For example, numbers may be encoded as if they had optional leading zeros. Implementations of decoders must support all possible alternatives; implementations of encoders can pick any allowed encoding.

The recommended extension for files containing WebAssembly modules in binary format is “`\mathtt{.wasm}`” and the recommended [Media Type](https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/media-types.xhtml) is “`\mathtt{application/wasm}`”.

\[1\]

Additional encoding layers – for example, introducing compression – may be defined on top of the basic representation defined here. However, such layers are outside the scope of the current specification.

## Grammar

The following conventions are adopted in defining grammar rules for the binary format. They mirror the conventions used for abstract syntax. In order to distinguish symbols of the binary syntax from symbols of the abstract syntax, `{\mathtt{typewriter}}` font is adopted for the former.

- Terminal symbols are bytes expressed in hexadecimal notation: `\mathtt{0x0F}`.

- Nonterminal symbols are written in typewriter font: `{\mathtt{valtype}}`, `{\mathtt{instr}}`.

- `{B^{n}}` is a sequence of `n \geq 0` iterations of `B`.

- `{B^\ast}` is a possibly empty sequence of iterations of `B`. (This is a shorthand for `{B^{n}}` used where `n` is not relevant.)

- `{B^?}` is an optional occurrence of `B`. (This is a shorthand for `{B^{n}}` where `n \leq 1`.)

- `x{:}B` denotes the same language as the nonterminal `B`, but also binds the variable `x` to the attribute synthesized for `B`. A pattern may also be used instead of a variable, e.g., `7{:}B`.

- Productions are written `\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}r@{~}r@{~}l@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}} & {\mathtt{sym}} & ::= & B_1 ~\Rightarrow~ A_1 ~~|~~ \ldots ~~|~~ B_n ~\Rightarrow~ A_n \\ \end{array}`, where each `A_i` is the attribute that is synthesized for `{\mathtt{sym}}` in the given case, usually from attribute variables bound in `B_i`.

- Large productions may be split into multiple definitions, indicated by ending the first one with explicit ellipses, `\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}r@{~}r@{~}l@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}} & {\mathtt{sym}} & ::= & B_1 \\ \end{array}`, and starting continuations with ellipses, `\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}r@{~}r@{~}l@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}} & {\mathtt{sym}} & ::= & \dots ~~|~~ B_2 \\ \end{array}`.

- Some productions are augmented by side conditions in parentheses, which restrict the applicability of the production. They provide a shorthand for a combinatorial expansion of the production into many separate cases.

- If the same meta variable or non-terminal symbol appears multiple times in a production (in the syntax or in an attribute), then all those occurrences must have the same instantiation. (This is a shorthand for a side condition requiring multiple different variables to be equal.)

Note

For example, the binary grammar for number types is given as follows:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rrl@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathtt{numtype}} & ::= & \mathtt{0x7C} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & \mathsf{f\scriptstyle64} \\
    & & | & \mathtt{0x7D} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & \mathsf{f\scriptstyle32} \\
    & & | & \mathtt{0x7E} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & \mathsf{i\scriptstyle64} \\
    & & | & \mathtt{0x7F} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & \mathsf{i\scriptstyle32} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Consequently, the byte `\mathtt{0x7F}` encodes the type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}`, `\mathtt{0x7E}` encodes the type `\mathsf{i\scriptstyle64}`, and so forth. No other byte value is allowed as the encoding of a number type.

The binary grammar for limits is defined as follows:

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rrl@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathtt{limits}} & ::= & \mathtt{0x00}~~n{:}{\def\mathdef1499#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1499{\mathtt{64}}} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}, {}[ n \,{..}\, \epsilon ]) \\
    & & | & \mathtt{0x01}~~n{:}{\def\mathdef1499#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1499{\mathtt{64}}}~~m{:}{\def\mathdef1499#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1499{\mathtt{64}}} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle32}, {}[ n \,{..}\, m ]) \\
    & & | & \mathtt{0x04}~~n{:}{\def\mathdef1499#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1499{\mathtt{64}}} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle64}, {}[ n \,{..}\, \epsilon ]) \\
    & & | & \mathtt{0x05}~~n{:}{\def\mathdef1499#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1499{\mathtt{64}}}~~m{:}{\def\mathdef1499#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1499{\mathtt{64}}} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & (\mathsf{i\scriptstyle64}, {}[ n \,{..}\, m ]) \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

That is, a limits pair is encoded as either the byte `\mathtt{0x00}` followed by the encoding of a `{\mathit{u\scriptstyle\kern-0.1em64}}` value, or the byte `\mathtt{0x01}` followed by two such encodings. The variables `n` and `m` name the attributes of the respective `{\def\mathdef1499#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1499{\mathtt{64}}}` nonterminals, which in this case are the actual unsigned integers those decode into. The attribute of the complete production then is the abstract syntax for the limit, expressed in terms of the former values.

## Auxiliary Notation

When dealing with binary encodings the following notation is also used:

- `\epsilon` denotes the empty byte sequence.

- `||{\mathtt{B}}||` is the length of the byte sequence generated from the production `{\mathtt{B}}` in a derivation.

## Lists

Lists are encoded with their `{\def\mathdef1498#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1498{\mathtt{32}}}` length followed by the encoding of their element sequence.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rrl@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathtt{list}}({\mathtt{X}}) & ::= & n{:}{\def\mathdef1498#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1498{\mathtt{32}}}~~{({\mathit{el}}{:}{\mathtt{X}})^{n}} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & {{\mathit{el}}^{n}} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

# Values

## Bytes

Bytes encode themselves.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rrl@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}}
    & {\mathtt{byte}} & ::= & \mathtt{0x00} ~~|~~ \ldots ~~|~~ \mathtt{0xFF} \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

## Integers

All integers are encoded using the [LEB128](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LEB128) variable-length integer encoding, in either unsigned or signed variant.

Unsigned integers are encoded in [unsigned LEB128](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LEB128#Unsigned_LEB128) format. As an additional constraint, the total number of bytes encoding a `{{\mathit{u}\kern-0.1em}}{N}` value must not exceed `{\mathrm{ceil}}(N / 7)` bytes.

    \begin{split}\begin{array}[t]{@{}l@{}rrl@{}l@{}l@{}l@{}}
    & {{\def\mathdef1649#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1649{}}}{N} & ::= & n{:}{\mathtt{byte}} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & n & \quad \mbox{if}~ n < {2^{7}} \land n < {2^{N}} \\
    & & | & n{:}{\mathtt{byte}}~~m{:}{{\def\mathdef1649#1{{\mathtt{u}#1}}\mathdef1649{}}}{(N - 7)} & \quad\Rightarrow\quad{} & {2^{7}} \cdot m + (n - {2^{7}}) & \quad \mbox{if}~ n \geq {2^{7}} \land N > 7 \\
    \end{array}\end{split}

Signed integers are encoded in [signed LEB128](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LEB128#Signed_LEB128) format, which uses a two’s complement representation.
